## The composer-audit component [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-composer-audit.html#the-composer-audit-component)

Fresh eyes on the manifest: this component runs `composer audit --locked` and fails the pipeline on advisories. This page shows how to add the `composer-audit` component to your app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`, then how to run it on a weekly schedule so the check keeps running after code is merged.

### Include the component [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-composer-audit.html#include-the-component)

Goal: your app's pipeline fails whenever a locked dependency has a known advisory. Add the include to your app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/composer-audit@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
    inputs:
      working_dir: .
```

### Inputs [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-composer-audit.html#inputs)

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `composer-audit` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `composer:2.11.1@sha256:8de2184c6de224f4689e8f80ed5f5edaf0030b6b8b7839a22a2bcb6722ac87d0` | Docker image for the job. |
| `image_prefix` | string | `${CI_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GROUP_IMAGE_PREFIX}` | Registry path in front of `image`: the job pulls `image_prefix/image`. The default is the group's GitLab Dependency Proxy, so Docker Hub is asked once and GitLab serves the cached copy. Outside a group with the proxy, set `docker.io`. No trailing slash. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Directory to run composer audit in, relative to the project root. |
| `abandoned` | string | `fail` | How composer audit treats abandoned packages: fail (default), report (list them, do not fail) or ignore. |

Note

The template adds regexes to three inputs: `job_name` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$`, `working_dir` must match `^(\.|[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9._/-]*)$` and `abandoned` must match `^(fail|report|ignore)$`.

### What the job does [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-composer-audit.html#what-the-job-does)

The Composer image (`composer:2.11.1`, pinned by digest) already ships Composer, so no install step is needed. The job is `interruptible: true` with a `timeout: 30 minutes`. Its script changes into `working_dir` and runs `composer audit --locked` with `--abandoned` set to the `abandoned` input (see Abandoned packages below). The command exits non-zero when it finds advisories, which fails the job.

Warning

The component carries no `allow_failure` input on purpose: a known advisory must fail the pipeline.

### What fails the job [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-composer-audit.html#what-fails-the-job)

`composer audit --locked` reads only the lock file (it installs nothing) and fails the job on any of three findings:

- **A security advisory** on a locked version. This fails in every mode.
- **A malware-flagged version.** Composer 2.10 also reads the filter lists a repository publishes; Packagist publishes one, `malware`, fed by Aikido. The job log names the package, the list, the source and a `PKFE-` ID. This fails in every mode too: the `abandoned` input does not touch it.
- **An abandoned package**, while `abandoned` is `fail` (see below).

Composer asks Packagist for advisories and filter lists on every run, so the job needs outbound HTTPS to packagist.org. When Packagist cannot be reached the job fails rather than passes: the component never adds `--ignore-unreachable`.

Preflight's own pipeline keeps these promises with the `must-fail-composer-audit` job: it runs this template's own lines on a clean app (must pass) and on three fixed locks, laravel/framework v9.0.0 (CVE-2024-52301), aikido/endpoint-test 0.0.1 (Aikido's harmless package, flagged on purpose so scanners can be tested) and an abandoned package, which must fail (the abandoned one only in `fail` mode). A flight check that has never seen a red light is just a light.

### Abandoned packages [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-composer-audit.html#abandoned-packages)

An abandoned package is one its author no longer maintains; Composer marks it in the lock file. By default an abandoned package in the lock fails the job, and the component keeps that default: `fail` is what the `abandoned` input holds when you set nothing.

The three modes:

- `fail` (default): the job fails when the lock holds an abandoned package.
- `report`: the job lists the abandoned packages but does not fail on them.
- `ignore`: the job does not look at abandoned packages at all.

`report` is the right choice for an old app that carries abandoned transitive packages it cannot upgrade yet: the pipeline stays green while the job log names every abandoned package, so the debt is visible instead of hidden. Advisories still fail the job in every mode: `abandoned` relaxes only the abandoned check, never the advisory check.

### Run it on a schedule [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-composer-audit.html#run-it-on-a-schedule)

New advisories are published after code is merged, so a green pipeline today can be stale tomorrow. Create a weekly pipeline schedule on the default branch: project settings, Build, Pipeline schedules. The component needs nothing extra; it carries no `rules:` block, so it runs in scheduled pipelines like any other. Creating the schedule is a project setting, not a file in the app's repo, and someone with Maintainer rights on the app must do it. It is the one Preflight check that books its own flight time.

### Related [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-composer-audit.html#related)

- [The proctor component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-proctor.html)
- [The php-test component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-php-test.html)

---

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-eslint.html

## The eslint component [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-eslint.html#the-eslint-component)

This page covers the `eslint` component: what the job does, how to include it, and every input it takes. Goal: the app's pipeline fails on any lint or format error, judged by the app's own config. Start with the include block, then check the inputs against your app. Preflight is named for the pre-flight check, and this component is the row that keeps the JavaScript airworthy.

Version 1 · Category: Testing/Validation · Tags: javascript,style,eslint,prettier

### What the job does [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-eslint.html#what-the-job-does)

The component runs the app's own [ESLint](https://eslint.org/) (and [Prettier](https://prettier.io/)) and fails the pipeline on lint or format errors. It does not install ESLint or Prettier itself: the app must require `@waynestate/pinstripe`, `eslint` and `prettier` as dev dependencies and ship an `eslint.config.js` (or point `eslint_args` at its own files).

The job, in order:

1. Moves into `working_dir` (default `.`).
2. Installs the app's dependencies with `npm ci --ignore-scripts --cache .npm-cache`.
3. Runs `npx --no-install eslint` with `eslint_args` (default `.`).
4. When `prettier` is `true` (the default), runs `npx --no-install prettier --check .`.

The job caches npm downloads in `.npm-cache/`, with the cache key based on `package-lock.json`. It is interruptible and times out after 15m.

### Include the component [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-eslint.html#include-the-component)

Add the include to the app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`, pinned to a full commit SHA with the tag in a trailing comment:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/eslint@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
    inputs:
      eslint_args: .
```

### Inputs [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-eslint.html#inputs)

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `eslint` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `node:22.13-alpine@sha256:e2b39f7b64281324929257d0f8004fb6cb4bf0fdfb9aa8cedb235a766aec31da` | Docker image for the job. |
| `image_prefix` | string | `${CI_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GROUP_IMAGE_PREFIX}` | Registry path in front of `image`: the job pulls `image_prefix/image`. The default is the group's GitLab Dependency Proxy, so Docker Hub is asked once and GitLab serves the cached copy. Outside a group with the proxy, set `docker.io`. No trailing slash. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Directory to run the commands in, relative to the project root. |
| `eslint_args` | string | `.` | Arguments passed to eslint. |
| `prettier` | boolean | `true` | Whether to also run `prettier --check`. |

### Verify [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-eslint.html#verify)

Push the change. The `eslint` job lands in the `test` stage by default, and a green job means ESLint and Prettier found nothing to fix.

Note

The `eslint` job has no `allow_failure` input: a lint or format error fails the pipeline.

### Related [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-eslint.html#related)

- [Quick start](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html): wire one component into an app and watch the pipeline run it.
- [Install](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html): the requirements, the include snippet, and how to verify.
- [The phpstan component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-phpstan.html): the static analysis check for the PHP side.
- [Include a component twice](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/include-twice.html): the `job_name` input in action.
- [Reference](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html): every component, with its inputs and defaults.

## The npm-audit component [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-npm-audit.html#the-npm-audit-component)

The front-end half of [composer-audit](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-composer-audit.html): this component runs `npm audit` on the app's `package-lock.json` and fails the pipeline on an advisory at or above `audit_level` (`high` by default) in a runtime dependency. Then it prints a full report, dev dependencies included, that never fails. This page shows how to add it, what each input does, and how CREED's severity words map to npm's.

### Include the component [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-npm-audit.html#include-the-component)

Goal: your app's pipeline fails whenever a locked runtime npm package has a known high or critical advisory. Add the include to your app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/npm-audit@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
    inputs:
      working_dir: .
```

npm-audit ships in Preflight 0.5.0; 0.4.0 does not include it. Pin that tag's full commit SHA, with the tag in a trailing comment, or the full commit SHA of a commit at or after it. The [Upgrading](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html) page has the 0.5.0 checklist.

### Inputs [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-npm-audit.html#inputs)

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `npm-audit` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `node:22.13-alpine@sha256:e2b39f7b64281324929257d0f8004fb6cb4bf0fdfb9aa8cedb235a766aec31da` | Docker image for the job: the same Node image and digest the `eslint` component pins. |
| `image_prefix` | string | `${CI_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GROUP_IMAGE_PREFIX}` | Registry path in front of `image`: the job pulls `image_prefix/image`. The default is the group's GitLab Dependency Proxy, so Docker Hub is asked once and GitLab serves the cached copy. Outside a group with the proxy, set `docker.io`. No trailing slash. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Directory that holds `package-lock.json`, relative to the project root. |
| `audit_level` | string | `high` | Lowest severity that fails the job: `low`, `moderate`, `high` or `critical`. `medium` is accepted too and means `moderate` (see Severity words below). |
| `omit_dev` | boolean | `true` | Whether the failing audit leaves dev dependencies out. The full report after it always lists them and never fails. |

Note

The template adds regexes to three inputs: `job_name` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$`, `working_dir` must match `^(\.|[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9._/-]*)$` and `audit_level` must match `^(low|moderate|medium|high|critical)$`.

### What the job does [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-npm-audit.html#what-the-job-does)

The job is `interruptible: true` with a `timeout: 10 minutes`. Its script changes into `working_dir`, then:

1. **No lock, nothing to audit.** With no `package-lock.json` (or `npm-shrinkwrap.json`) the job prints `npm-audit: no lock file (package-lock.json or npm-shrinkwrap.json) in <dir>, nothing to audit.` and passes. An app with no front end never goes red.
2. **The gate.** `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=<audit_level> --audit=true --offline=false` (no `--omit=dev` when `omit_dev` is `false`). npm exits non-zero on an advisory at or above the level, and the job keeps that exit code.
3. **The full report.** When `omit_dev` is `true`, a second `npm audit` lists every finding, dev dependencies included, and never fails the job. A dev-only finding shows up in the log without stopping the merge.

`npm audit` reads only the lock. Nothing is installed, so no package's install script runs in this job.

Warning

The component carries no `allow_failure` input on purpose: an advisory at or above `audit_level` must fail the pipeline. To let one advisory through while a fix lands, raise `audit_level` for a short time and say why in the merge request, or move the package to a fixed version.

#### Why `--audit=true --offline=false` [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-npm-audit.html#why-audit-true-offline-false)

An app's own `.npmrc` can carry `audit=false` or `offline=true`. Either one makes `npm audit` skip the request, print `found 0 vulnerabilities` and exit 0: a pass that audited nothing. The two flags override the file, so the job always asks the registry.

#### When the registry cannot be reached [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-npm-audit.html#when-the-registry-cannot-be-reached)

`npm audit` posts the lock's package tree to the registry's audit endpoint, so the job needs outbound HTTPS to the registry (`registry.npmjs.org` unless the app's `.npmrc` names another). When the endpoint cannot be reached, or the registry does not offer one, npm exits non-zero with `audit endpoint returned an error`, and the job adds `npm-audit: the registry's audit endpoint could not be reached or refused the request, so nothing was audited.` It fails rather than passes unchecked. A private registry that proxies npm must also serve npm's audit endpoints (`/-/npm/v1/security/advisories/bulk`, with `/-/npm/v1/security/audits/quick` as npm's fallback), or the job fails on every run.

### Severity words [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-npm-audit.html#severity-words)

CREED's policy (`rules.audit_severity_threshold` in `policy.json`, read by PROCTOR) and Composer use `low`, `medium`, `high` and `critical`. npm uses `low`, `moderate`, `high` and `critical` (plus `info` and `none`, which this component does not accept: `none` would never fail and `info` fails on notes). The map:

| CREED and Composer | npm (`--audit-level`) |
| --- | --- |
| `low` | `low` |
| `medium` | `moderate` |
| `high` | `high` |
| `critical` | `critical` |

So `audit_level` takes the policy's value as it is: `audit_level: medium` runs `npm audit --audit-level=moderate`, and the log says `failing on moderate or higher`. The default, `high`, matches the stack policy's `audit_severity_threshold`.

### Caching [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-npm-audit.html#caching)

The job installs nothing, but npm fetches package metadata while it reports. It reads the app's own npm cache: the fixed key `npm` and the path `.cache/npm/` (`npm_config_cache` points there), the ones Sourdough's generated pipelines use, with `policy: pull`. The audit never uploads, so an audit running next to the app's install job cannot overwrite the packages that job just downloaded. In an app with no npm cache of its own the job simply starts cold.

### Proof [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-npm-audit.html#proof)

Preflight's own pipeline keeps these promises with the `must-fail-npm-audit` job. It runs this template's own script on fixed locks: lodash 4.17.20 (GHSA-35jh-r3h4-6jhm, high) fails at `high` and `medium` and passes at `critical`, an `.npmrc` that turns the audit off still fails, the same lodash as a dev dependency fails only with `omit_dev: false`, a clean lock and an app with no lock pass, and an unreachable registry fails a clean lock. The pipeline also includes the component on the clean fixture, where it must pass. A smoke detector is only worth the batteries if someone pressed the test button.

### Run it on a schedule [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-npm-audit.html#run-it-on-a-schedule)

New advisories are published after code is merged. The weekly pipeline schedule from [composer-audit](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-composer-audit.html#run-it-on-a-schedule) covers this job too: it carries no `rules:` block, so it runs in scheduled pipelines like any other.

### Related [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-npm-audit.html#related)

- [The composer-audit component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-composer-audit.html)
- [The eslint component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-eslint.html)
- [Dependency caching](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/dependency-caching.html)

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-package-publish.html

## The package-publish component [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-package-publish.html#the-package-publish-component)

This page covers the `package-publish` component: what the job does, how to include it, and every input it takes. Goal: tagging a release publishes the package to the GitLab group's built-in Composer registry, and a version that is already published never gets overwritten.

Version 1 · Category: Release/Publishing · Tags: composer,publish,release

### What the job does [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-package-publish.html#what-the-job-does)

The job publishes a semantic version tag to the GitLab group's built-in Composer registry. It runs only on tags, reads the registry first, and refuses a moved version: a version already published from this commit passes quietly, and a version published from a different commit fails the pipeline, because GitLab would otherwise overwrite it without a word. Once a version is on the manifest, it stays on the manifest: no go-arounds.

The job, in order:

1. Runs only when the pipeline is for a tag, so `$CI_COMMIT_TAG` is set.
2. Accepts only semantic versions, `1.2.3` or `v1.2.3` with an optional pre-release; any other tag fails the job.
3. Reads the package name from the `name` field of `composer.json` in the project root, the file the registry serves.
4. Reads the registry index with the read token. A `404` means the group has no published Composer packages yet, and the job goes straight to publishing.
5. Compares the commit recorded for the version, if any, with `$CI_COMMIT_SHA`: the same commit exits quietly, a different commit fails the job instead of overwriting the version.
6. Publishes the tag to the group's registry with the job token (`CI_JOB_TOKEN`) and reports the version as published.

The default image ships curl and PHP, which the job uses for the registry round trip. The job is interruptible and times out after 30 minutes.

Warning

Protect your release tags.

Note

The read token lives in a masked CI variable named by `read_token_variable` (default `PACKAGE_READ_TOKEN`) and needs the `read_package_registry` scope. Publishing itself uses the predefined `CI_JOB_TOKEN`.

### Include the component [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-package-publish.html#include-the-component)

Add the include to the app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`, pinned to a full commit SHA with the tag in a trailing comment, and set `group_id` to the numeric id of the GitLab group whose built-in Composer registry hosts the package:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/package-publish@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
    inputs:
      group_id: "<your group id>"
```

### Inputs [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-package-publish.html#inputs)

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `deploy` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `package-publish` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `composer:2.11.1@sha256:8de2184c6de224f4689e8f80ed5f5edaf0030b6b8b7839a22a2bcb6722ac87d0` | Docker image for the job. The default ships curl and PHP, which the job uses for the registry round trip. |
| `image_prefix` | string | `${CI_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GROUP_IMAGE_PREFIX}` | Registry path in front of `image`: the job pulls `image_prefix/image`. The default is the group's GitLab Dependency Proxy, so Docker Hub is asked once and GitLab serves the cached copy. Outside a group with the proxy, set `docker.io`. No trailing slash. |
| `group_id` | string | none | Numeric id of the GitLab group whose built-in Composer registry hosts the package. Required. |
| `read_token_variable` | string | `PACKAGE_READ_TOKEN` | Name of the masked CI variable holding a token with the `read_package_registry` scope, used to read the registry before publishing. |

### Verify [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-package-publish.html#verify)

Define the masked CI variable the component reads, then push a semantic version tag. Expected: the `package-publish` job runs in the `deploy` stage, reads the registry, and ends with `Version <version> published.` Pushing the same tag from the same commit again exits quietly; the same version from a different commit fails the job.

### Related [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-package-publish.html#related)

- [Quick start](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html): wire one component into an app and watch the pipeline run it.
- [Install](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html): the requirements, the include snippet, and how to verify.
- [When the components run](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/when-components-run.html): the `workflow:rules` block that belongs in the app's own file.
- [Include a component twice](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/include-twice.html): the `job_name` input in action.
- [Reference](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html): every component, with its inputs and defaults.

## The php-test component [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-php-test.html#the-php-test-component)

Every engine gets its own check: this component runs your test command once per supported PHP version. This page shows how to add the `php-test` component to your app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`, how the matrix and the cache work, and how to trial the next PHP release. Next, add the [composer-audit component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-composer-audit.html).

### Include the component [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-php-test.html#include-the-component)

Goal: your app's test suite runs on each supported PHP version. The component runs the test command on each supported PHP version through `parallel:matrix`. Add the include to your app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
    inputs:
      test_command: vendor/bin/phpunit
```

### Inputs [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-php-test.html#inputs)

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the jobs. |
| `job_name` | string | `php-test` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `php:${PHP_VERSION}-cli-trixie` | Docker image for the jobs. The default carries the literal `${PHP_VERSION}`, which GitLab expands in the image at job time. |
| `image_prefix` | string | `${CI_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GROUP_IMAGE_PREFIX}` | Registry path in front of `image`: the job pulls `image_prefix/image`. The default is the group's GitLab Dependency Proxy, so Docker Hub is asked once and GitLab serves the cached copy. Outside a group with the proxy, set `docker.io`. No trailing slash. |
| `php_versions` | array | `["8.3", "8.4", "8.5"]` | PHP versions to test against. |
| `php_advisory_version` | string | `""` | One more PHP version tested in a separate `<job_name>-advisory` job that may fail (`allow_failure: true`), for a release candidate. Empty: no advisory job. Never add a release candidate to `php_versions`. |
| `composer_version` | string | `2.11.1` | Composer version to install, 2.9.6 or later. |
| `test_command` | string | `vendor/bin/phpunit` | The test command to run. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Directory to run the command in, relative to the project root. |

Note

The template adds regexes to three inputs: `job_name` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$`, `composer_version` must match `^2\.(9\.([6-9]|[1-9][0-9]+)|[1-9][0-9]+\.[0-9]+)$`, and `working_dir` must match `^(\.|[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9._/-]*)$`.

### What the jobs do [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-php-test.html#what-the-jobs-do)

The array input feeds `parallel:matrix` directly, so one job is created per PHP version. `PHP_VERSION` becomes a CI/CD variable in each job, which the `image` input's default expands at job time. The default image is deliberately tag-pinned, so each job runs the newest patch release of its PHP version. Each job is `interruptible: true` with a `timeout: 30 minutes`, and its script:

1. Installs `unzip` and `git` with `apt-get`, because the `php:*-cli` images do not ship them (the images are Debian-based, so `apt` is used).
2. Copies the official Composer installer from `getcomposer.org` and verifies its SHA-384 against the signature fetched at runtime from `composer.github.io/installer.sig`. On a mismatch the check deletes the installer and exits 1. No `$` variables appear in the `php -r` code, so GitLab CI variable expansion cannot corrupt it.
3. Runs the installer quietly with `--install-dir=/usr/local/bin --filename=composer` and the pinned `composer_version`, so Composer lands on PATH, then removes `composer-setup.php`.
4. Changes into `working_dir` and runs `composer install --no-interaction --no-progress`.
5. Runs `test_command`.

### Caching [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-php-test.html#caching)

The jobs always cache Composer downloads in `.composer-cache/` so repeat runs do not re-download every package. The cache key is fixed per PHP version, not a `composer.lock` hash, so a lock change downloads only the packages that changed and each PHP version gets its own cache:

```yaml
cache:
  key: preflight-php-${PHP_VERSION}
  paths:
    - .composer-cache/
  policy: pull-push
variables:
  COMPOSER_CACHE_DIR: "$CI_PROJECT_DIR/.composer-cache"
```

`COMPOSER_CACHE_DIR` points Composer at a path inside the project so GitLab can cache it.

### Try the next PHP release without breaking the pipeline [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-php-test.html#try-the-next-php-release-without-breaking-the-pipeline)

Include `php-test` a second time for the release that is not supported yet, name that job, and let it fail. The name is what lets your own `.gitlab-ci.yml` loosen only that job:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@<full commit SHA> # <tag>
    inputs:
      php_versions: ["8.6"]
      job_name: php-test-next
      # While 8.6 only has release candidate images, name the tag: php:${PHP_VERSION}-rc-cli-trixie
      # image: "php:${PHP_VERSION}-rc-cli-trixie"

php-test-next:
  allow_failure: true
```

A red `php-test-next` job is an early warning, not a stop. Drop the `allow_failure` and move the version into the main `php_versions` list once the release is supported (the supported versions follow `policy.json`).

### Testing the next PHP release [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-php-test.html#testing-the-next-php-release)

Set `php_advisory_version` to a release candidate tag and the component adds a `<job_name>-advisory` job that runs your tests on that version:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
    inputs:
      test_command: vendor/bin/phpunit
      php_advisory_version: "8.6.0RC2"
```

The job warns, it never blocks; move the version into `php_versions` only once it is a final, supported release.

### Related [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-php-test.html#related)

- [The proctor component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-proctor.html)
- [The composer-audit component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-composer-audit.html)

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-phpstan.html

## The phpstan component [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-phpstan.html#the-phpstan-component)

This page shows how to add the `phpstan` component to an app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`: it runs the app's own [PHPStan](https://phpstan.org/) and fails the pipeline on static analysis errors, writing a GitLab Code Quality report. It finds the loose bolts before the flight does; check the requirements first, then add the include.

Version 1, category Testing/Validation, tags `php`, `static-analysis`, `phpstan`.

### Before you start [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-phpstan.html#before-you-start)

The component does not install PHPStan itself. The app must:

- Require `phpstan/phpstan` as a dev dependency.
- Ship a `phpstan.neon`, or point the `config` input at its own file.

### Include the component [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-phpstan.html#include-the-component)

Add the include to the app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`, pinned to a commit SHA with the tag in a trailing comment:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/phpstan@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
    inputs:
      config: phpstan.neon
      memory_limit: 1G
```

A tag or branch can move; a SHA cannot.

### What the job does [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-phpstan.html#what-the-job-does)

The job lands in the `test` stage by default, is `interruptible: true`, and has a `timeout: 10m`. It runs three steps:

1. Move to the directory given by `working_dir` (default `.`).
2. Install the app's dependencies:
   ```sh
   composer install --no-interaction --no-progress --prefer-dist
   ```
3. Run PHPStan against the app's own config:
   ```sh
   vendor/bin/phpstan analyse --no-progress --error-format=gitlab --memory-limit=1G -c phpstan.neon > "$CI_PROJECT_DIR/phpstan-report.json"
   ```
   - `--memory-limit` takes the `memory_limit` input (default `1G`).
   - `-c` takes the `config` input (default `phpstan.neon`).
   - `--error-format=gitlab` writes the findings as a GitLab Code Quality report to `$CI_PROJECT_DIR/phpstan-report.json`.

### Report [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-phpstan.html#report)

The job publishes the report as a Code Quality report:

```yaml
artifacts:
  when: always
  reports:
    codequality: phpstan-report.json
```

### Inputs [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-phpstan.html#inputs)

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `phpstan` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `composer:2.11.1@sha256:8de2184c6de224f4689e8f80ed5f5edaf0030b6b8b7839a22a2bcb6722ac87d0` | Docker image for the job. |
| `image_prefix` | string | `${CI_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GROUP_IMAGE_PREFIX}` | Registry path in front of `image`: the job pulls `image_prefix/image`. The default is the group's GitLab Dependency Proxy, so Docker Hub is asked once and GitLab serves the cached copy. Outside a group with the proxy, set `docker.io`. No trailing slash. |
| `config` | string | `phpstan.neon` | Path to the app's PHPStan config file. It must be a relative path; GitLab refuses the pipeline at creation if it is not. |
| `memory_limit` | string | `1G` | Memory limit passed to PHPStan. A PHP size such as `1G`, `512M` or `-1`; GitLab refuses the pipeline at creation if it is not. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Directory to run PHPStan in, relative to the project root. |

`job_name` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$`, and `working_dir` must match `^(\.|[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9._/-]*)$`.

Note

`config` must be a relative path, and `memory_limit` takes a PHP size such as `1G`, `512M` or `-1`. Each carries an input `regex`, so GitLab refuses the pipeline at creation when a value does not match.

### Verify [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-phpstan.html#verify)

Push the change. The components are ordinary jobs, so the `phpstan` job runs whenever the app's pipeline runs, in the `test` stage by default. A green job means no static analysis errors, and the Code Quality report carries the findings.

### Related [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-phpstan.html#related)

- [The pint component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-pint.html): the style check that pairs with it.
- [The proctor component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-proctor.html): another check that publishes a Code Quality report.
- [Include a component twice](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/include-twice.html): the `job_name` input when one project includes the same component more than once.
- [Reference](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html): every component, with its inputs and defaults.

## The pint component [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-pint.html#the-pint-component)

This page shows how to add the `pint` component to an app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`: it runs the app's own [Laravel Pint](https://laravel.com/docs/12.x/pint) in test mode and fails the pipeline on style errors. It is the cockpit polish (every line tidied before takeoff); check the requirements first, then add the include.

Version 1, category Testing/Validation, tags `php`, `style`, `pint`.

### Before you start [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-pint.html#before-you-start)

The component does not install Pint itself. The app must:

- Require `laravel/pint` as a dev dependency.
- Ship a `pint.json`, or point the `config` input at its own file.

### Include the component [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-pint.html#include-the-component)

Add the include to the app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`, pinned to a commit SHA with the tag in a trailing comment:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/pint@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
    inputs:
      config: pint.json
```

A tag or branch can move; a SHA cannot.

### What the job does [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-pint.html#what-the-job-does)

The job lands in the `test` stage by default, is `interruptible: true`, and has a `timeout: 10m`. It runs three steps:

1. Move to the directory given by `working_dir` (default `.`).
2. Install the app's dependencies:
   ```sh
   composer install --no-interaction --no-progress --prefer-dist
   ```
3. Run Pint in test mode against the app's own config:
   ```sh
   vendor/bin/pint --test --config=pint.json
   ```
   `--config` takes the `config` input (default `pint.json`). A style error fails the job, and with it the pipeline.

### Inputs [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-pint.html#inputs)

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `pint` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `composer:2.11.1@sha256:8de2184c6de224f4689e8f80ed5f5edaf0030b6b8b7839a22a2bcb6722ac87d0` | Docker image for the job. |
| `image_prefix` | string | `${CI_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GROUP_IMAGE_PREFIX}` | Registry path in front of `image`: the job pulls `image_prefix/image`. The default is the group's GitLab Dependency Proxy, so Docker Hub is asked once and GitLab serves the cached copy. Outside a group with the proxy, set `docker.io`. No trailing slash. |
| `config` | string | `pint.json` | Path to the app's Pint config file. It must be a relative path; GitLab refuses the pipeline at creation if it is not. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Directory to run Pint in, relative to the project root. |

`job_name` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$`, and `working_dir` must match `^(\.|[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9._/-]*)$`.

Note

`config` must be a relative path. The input carries a `regex`, so GitLab refuses the pipeline at creation when a value does not match.

### Verify [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-pint.html#verify)

Push the change. The components are ordinary jobs, so the `pint` job runs whenever the app's pipeline runs, in the `test` stage by default. A green job means the app's code is clean under its own Pint config.

### Related [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-pint.html#related)

- [The phpstan component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-phpstan.html): the static analysis check that pairs with it.
- [The eslint component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-eslint.html): the JavaScript style check.
- [Include a component twice](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/include-twice.html): the `job_name` input when one project includes the same component more than once.
- [Reference](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html): every component, with its inputs and defaults.

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-portability.html

## The portability component [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-portability.html#the-portability-component)

The portability component proves your app image runs anywhere a container platform runs it: OpenShift, Coolify, plain Docker, and Citadel too. It builds the image, boots it twice side by side as a stranger (an arbitrary uid with no name, in group 0, with no capabilities), and runs the six checks from ADR-0010 plus the image's own HEALTHCHECK. Like the real pre-flight, it is a list you finish on the ground: if one light is red, nobody taxis.

### What it checks [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-portability.html#what-it-checks)

The strict boot comes first, because every other check stands on it. Then the seven checks, each reported on its own line.

| Check | What it does | What a failure usually means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `strict-boot` | Starts the image as `uid:0` (default `100123:0`) with no `/etc/passwd` entry and every capability dropped. Fails if the app root is writable by that user, if a writable path is missing or not writable by group 0, if the second replica does not listen on the port its `port_env` variable names, or if the app wrote anywhere outside `writable_paths` and `runtime_paths` while it ran (what a read-only root filesystem would refuse). | The image expects root, a named user, a fixed port, or writes caches next to the code. |
| `health` | Asks for `health_path` with a bare IP address in `Host` (`Host: <ip>:<port>`), no forwarded headers, at the job's own address, and expects 200. That is what a platform's probe sends. | Trusted-host lists, HTTPS redirects, sessions or auth run before the health route. |
| `env-only` | Fails on a `.env` file or a Laravel config cache (`bootstrap/cache/config.php`) baked into the image; the app must boot on the `env` input alone. | Config was copied or cached at build time. |
| `forwarded-headers` | Requests `probe_path` twice: plain, then with forged `X-Forwarded-Host`, `-Proto`, `-Port` and the `identity_header`, sent from an untrusted peer. Fails if the status or `Location` changes or a forged value shows up in the answer. | The app trusts every proxy, so anyone can set its host, scheme or user. |
| `logs` | Fails if nothing reached stdout or stderr during the run, or if anything was written under `logs_path` (default `storage/logs`). | Logs go to files that vanish with the container. |
| `session-hop` | Signs in on replica A with `session_login_path`, then sends that cookie to replica B's `session_check_path` and expects 200. The replicas have separate disks. | Sessions live in local files instead of a shared store or a signed cookie. |
| `sigterm` | Sends SIGTERM to the main process and expects it to exit by itself within `stop_timeout` seconds, as PID 1 must. | The process has no SIGTERM handler (PID 1 ignores the signal by default), or the handler hangs. |
| `healthcheck` | Runs the image's own `HEALTHCHECK` command, if it declares one, inside replica A as the app's uid with the same environment, up to three times two seconds apart, and expects exit 0. Fails when the command exits non-zero, or when the image declares no HEALTHCHECK and `require_healthcheck` is true. | The image's own health command fails, so Docker and Coolify would mark the container unhealthy. |

The job prints one `portability: <check>: problem: ...` line per problem as it finds it, then a summary with `pass`, `FAIL` or `skipped` for every check, and passes only when every check that ran passed.

### Add the include [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-portability.html#add-the-include)

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/portability@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
    inputs:
      env: ["APP_KEY=${PORTABILITY_APP_KEY}", "APP_URL=https://myapp.example.edu", "SESSION_DRIVER=cookie", "LOG_CHANNEL=stderr"]
      session_login_path: /_portability/login
      session_check_path: /_portability/me
```

Note

The one-job component on this page ships in 0.2.0. 0.1.4 carries an earlier two-job version (`portability-build` and `portability-run`, checked with goss); see [Upgrading](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html). Pin the full commit SHA of the release tag you use.

With no `start_command`, the job runs the image's own `ENTRYPOINT` and `CMD`, exactly as the platforms do. An Apache image (Squire's portable image, a Sourdough or WELD app) needs no `start_command` shim for Buildah: the job gives each replica stdio its uid owns and a process group of its own, as a container runtime does (see [What the job emulates](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-portability.html#what-the-job-emulates)). Put secrets such as `APP_KEY` in CI/CD variables and name them in `env`: `$NAME` and `${NAME}` in `env` and `build_args` values are replaced from the job's variables.

Warning

The runner must allow user namespaces, which Buildah's chroot isolation uses. Ordinary unprivileged Docker-executor runners do; no privileged mode, Docker-in-Docker or registry is needed.

#### A sign-in route for session-hop [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-portability.html#a-sign-in-route-for-session-hop)

`session-hop` needs a GET route that signs in a test user and one that answers 200 only when signed in. Enable them with an environment variable that only this job sets, so they never exist in production. In Laravel (and a Sourdough or WELD app):

```php
if (env('PORTABILITY_PROBE') === 'yes') {
    Route::middleware('web')->group(function () {
        Route::get('/_portability/login', function () {
            Auth::login(User::firstOrCreate(['email' => 'portability@example.invalid'], ['name' => 'Portability', 'password' => Str::random(40)]));

            return 'signed in';
        });
        Route::get('/_portability/me', fn () => Auth::check() ? 'ok' : abort(401));
    });
}
```

Add `"PORTABILITY_PROBE=yes"` to `env`. An app with no sign-in leaves `session-hop` out of `checks` on purpose; the other checks still run.

### How the job works [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-portability.html#how-the-job-works)

The component is one job, named by `job_name` (default `portability`). It runs in the Buildah image, pinned by digest, with `STORAGE_DRIVER=vfs` and `BUILDAH_ISOLATION=chroot`, `interruptible: true` and `timeout: 30 minutes`. In order, it:

1. Builds the image with `buildah bud`, from `dockerfile` in `context`, with `build_args`. It builds with `--format docker`, because Buildah's default OCI format drops the image's HEALTHCHECK and the docker format keeps it. Nothing is pushed: the image stays in the job's own storage.
2. Reads the image's `ENTRYPOINT` and `CMD`, makes two copies of its filesystem (replicas A and B) and runs the static parts of `strict-boot` and `env-only` on them.
3. Starts both replicas with `buildah run --user <uid>:0 --cap-drop=ALL` and the `env` input, each through a small launcher that gives it its own stdio and session; B gets `port + 1` through `port_env`.
4. Waits up to `boot_timeout` seconds for each replica's health path, then runs `health`, `env-only`, `forwarded-headers`, `session-hop`, `logs` and `sigterm` with curl.
5. Stops both replicas and compares what changed on disk against `writable_paths` and `runtime_paths`.

The probe is `templates/portability/probe.sh`, inlined in the template byte for byte, because a component ships only its `template.yml`. The inputs reach it through a quoted heredoc as data; nothing in them is run except `start_command`.

#### Why Buildah [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-portability.html#why-buildah)

The old runner allowed no Docker-in-Docker, and a privileged runner is a key to the building. Buildah is maintained by Red Hat, builds from a Dockerfile with no daemon, and can also run the image it built, as any uid, with no capabilities, inside an ordinary job. kaniko builds but cannot run a container, and Google archived it in 2025. A GitLab `services:` entry runs an image but cannot set its uid or drop its capabilities, and needs the image pushed to a registry first. Buildah needs neither a push nor a second job.

#### What the job emulates [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-portability.html#what-the-job-emulates)

The checks run in an unprivileged job, so a few things are emulated rather than enforced by a kernel. Each one fails the same apps the real thing would.

- **Read-only root.** The image is not mounted read-only; the job looks for files written outside the allowed paths after the run. A write is caught, not refused.
- **PID 1.** `buildah run` starts no PID namespace, so the main process is not PID 1. The job checks that it handles SIGTERM, and fails it when it dies of the signal's default action, which PID 1 would ignore.
- **No new privileges.** Every capability is dropped, but `buildah run` has no `no-new-privileges` flag. The uid has no passwd entry, so set-uid tools have little to grab.
- **Networking.** Both replicas share the job's network namespace; the second one listens on `port + 1`.
- **Stdio and process group.** On its own, `buildah run` differs from every container runtime twice. It hands the app stdout and stderr pipes owned by root, so an app running as the uid cannot reopen them (Apache fails with `could not open error log file /proc/self/fd/2`). And it starts no session, so the app shares a process group with `buildah-chroot-exec`, which runs as the same uid and SIGKILLs the app when the app signals its own group on SIGTERM (Apache's graceful stop does). runc and CRI-O do neither. So the job starts each replica through a launcher: it pipes stdout and stderr through `cat`, on a pipe the uid owns, then execs the app through `setsid`, keeping its pid, so the `sigterm` check still signals the app itself. The launcher uses the Buildah image's own `bash`, `setsid` and `cat` (its `/usr`, bind-mounted read-only at `/.preflight/usr` for the run only), so the app image needs none of them and nothing is written into it.

Note

Before 0.5.0 an Apache image needed a `start_command` shim such as `exec setsid bash -c 'exec > >(exec cat) 2>&1; exec <entrypoint>'`. Remove it when you upgrade: the job now does both itself, and a `setsid` inside the launcher's session forks the app away from the replica's main process, so `health` fails.

### Inputs [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-portability.html#inputs)

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the portability job. |
| `job_name` | string | `portability` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `quay.io/buildah/stable:v1.43.5-immutable@sha256:7c2b605262748ace2c5c57c5550942d0adad57aec82ede3070927722306c0ffb` | Buildah image the job runs in. It builds the app image and runs the probe, so it needs buildah, curl, awk and find. |
| `dockerfile` | string | `Dockerfile` | Dockerfile to build, relative to the context. |
| `context` | string | `.` | Build context, relative to the project root. |
| `build_args` | array | `[]` | Build arguments as `NAME=value`. `$NAME` and `${NAME}` in a value are replaced from the job's variables. |
| `app_root` | string | `/app` | Directory inside the image where the app lives. |
| `writable_paths` | array | `["storage", "bootstrap/cache"]` | Paths the app may write to, relative to `app_root`. Each must be writable by the uid in group 0. |
| `runtime_paths` | array | `["/tmp", "/var/tmp", "/run", "/var/run"]` | Absolute paths the platform mounts as tmpfs. Writes there are allowed. |
| `port` | number | `8080` | Port the app listens on by default. The second replica gets `port + 1` through `port_env`. |
| `port_env` | string | `PORT` | Environment variable that sets the app's listen port. |
| `health_path` | string | `/up` | Path that must answer 200 for any Host, before trusted hosts, HTTPS redirects, sessions and auth. |
| `uid` | number | `100123` | Numeric uid the app runs as, with no `/etc/passwd` entry. The gid is always 0. |
| `start_command` | string | `""` | Command that starts the app, run with `sh -c`. Empty runs the image's own `ENTRYPOINT` and `CMD`. |
| `env` | array | `[]` | Environment for both replicas, as `NAME=value` (or `NAME` to pass the job's variable through). Keep secrets in CI/CD variables. |
| `boot_timeout` | number | `60` | Seconds each replica has to answer the health path. |
| `stop_timeout` | number | `10` | Seconds the main process has to exit after SIGTERM. |
| `probe_path` | string | `/` | Page probed with and without forged forwarded headers; one that redirects or builds absolute URLs shows the most. |
| `identity_header` | string | `X-Forwarded-User` | Identity header a gateway would set (forged in `forwarded-headers`). |
| `session_login_path` | string | `""` | GET path that signs in a test user and sets the session cookie. Needed by `session-hop`. |
| `session_check_path` | string | `""` | Path that answers 200 only for a signed-in user. Needed by `session-hop`. |
| `logs_path` | string | `storage/logs` | Directory, relative to `app_root`, where nothing may be written. |
| `require_healthcheck` | boolean | `false` | Fail when the image declares no HEALTHCHECK. Docker and Coolify use it; OpenShift and Kubernetes use their own probes. |
| `checks` | array | `["health", "env-only", "forwarded-headers", "logs", "session-hop", "sigterm", "healthcheck"]` | The checks to run. Leave one out only on purpose; the strict boot always runs. |

The `image` default is an immutable tag (`-immutable`) pinned by digest, because the plain version tag can be re-pushed and its old digest removed.

### Verify locally [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-portability.html#verify-locally)

`tests/check-portability.sh` (and its `.ps1` twin) run the same probe in the same Buildah image against `tests/portability/app`: once clean, where every check must pass, and once per flaw (needs root, writes outside its paths, fixed port, host-bound health, a baked `.env`, trusts any proxy, file logs, file sessions, no SIGTERM handler, a failing HEALTHCHECK), where the targeted check must fail. Two more builds must pass every check: one reopens `/proc/self/fd/2` and one signals its whole process group on SIGTERM, as Apache does; they fail without the launcher. Preflight's own pipeline runs the component on the clean fixture and this check as `must-fail-portability`. See [Local checks](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/local-checks.html) for the commands.

### Related [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-portability.html#related)

- [Include a component twice](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/include-twice.html): the `job_name` input.
- [Same instance only](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/same-instance-only.html): components run only inside the GitLab instance that hosts this project.
- [When the components run](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/when-components-run.html): the `workflow:rules` block that belongs in the app's own file.

## The proctor component [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-proctor.html#the-proctor-component)

A proctor keeps an eye on the exam hall; this one keeps an eye on your app. This page shows how to add the `proctor` component to your app's `.gitlab-ci.yml` and what the job does once it runs. Next, add the [php-test component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-php-test.html) so the test suite runs on every supported PHP version.

### Include the component [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-proctor.html#include-the-component)

Goal: your app's pipeline runs PROCTOR and publishes the result as a GitLab Code Quality report. Add the include to your app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/proctor@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
    inputs:
      proctor_command: vendor/bin/proctor check --format=codequality
```

The job installs the app's dependencies with `composer install --no-plugins --no-scripts --ignore-platform-reqs`, so the app's plugins and scripts never run inside the job, and an app locked to an older PHP or needing an extension the image lacks (gd, oci8, ldap) still gets its report: the job reads the app and never runs it.

Note

The install skips plugins and scripts on purpose: the job only inspects the app, so nothing in the app runs with the job's access.

### Inputs [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-proctor.html#inputs)

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `proctor` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `php:8.4-cli-trixie@sha256:9cf851bc2c1b37c3e59dfd677a3c3e56d485af5a47c93f629424bb039eafcb69` | Docker image for the job. |
| `image_prefix` | string | `${CI_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GROUP_IMAGE_PREFIX}` | Registry path in front of `image`: the job pulls `image_prefix/image`. The default is the group's GitLab Dependency Proxy, so Docker Hub is asked once and GitLab serves the cached copy. Outside a group with the proxy, set `docker.io`. No trailing slash. |
| `composer_version` | string | `2.11.1` | Composer version to install, 2.9.6 or later. |
| `allow_failure` | boolean | `false` | Whether the job can fail without failing the pipeline. |
| `proctor_command` | string | `vendor/bin/proctor check --format=codequality` | The proctor command to run. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Directory to run the command in, relative to the project root. |
| `git_depth` | string | `"0"` | How many commits the job clones (GitLab's `GIT_DEPTH`); the default `0` clones the full history, so PROCTOR's override-approver check can see who wrote each override. |

Note

The template adds regexes to four inputs: `job_name` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$`, `composer_version` must match `^2\.(9\.([6-9]|[1-9][0-9]+)|[1-9][0-9]+\.[0-9]+)$`, `working_dir` must match `^(\.|[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9._/-]*)$`, and `git_depth` must match `^[0-9]+$`.

### What the job does [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-proctor.html#what-the-job-does)

The job is `interruptible: true` with a `timeout: 30 minutes`. Its script:

1. Installs `unzip` and `git` with `apt-get`, because the `php:8.4-cli-trixie` image does not ship them (the image is Debian-based, so `apt` is used).
2. Copies the official Composer installer from `getcomposer.org` and verifies its SHA-384 against the signature fetched at runtime from `composer.github.io/installer.sig`. On a mismatch the check deletes the installer and exits 1. No `$` variables appear in the `php -r` code, so GitLab CI variable expansion cannot corrupt it.
3. Runs the installer quietly with `--install-dir=/usr/local/bin --filename=composer` and the pinned `composer_version`, so Composer lands on PATH, then removes `composer-setup.php`.
4. Changes into `working_dir` and runs `composer install --no-interaction --no-progress --no-plugins --no-scripts --ignore-platform-reqs`.
5. Decides whether to add `--record` (see [Keep the JSON report for Rollcall](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-proctor.html#keep-the-json-report-for-rollcall)): only for a plain `proctor check` command whose PROCTOR lists `--record` in `check --help`.
6. Runs `proctor_command`, plus `--record "$CI_PROJECT_DIR/proctor.json"` when step 5 said so, and redirects the output to `"$CI_PROJECT_DIR/gl-code-quality-report.json"`. A plain redirect (not `tee`) keeps proctor's exit code as the job result, and the report is written at the project root so the artifact path is the same for every `working_dir`, including `.`.

The job keeps Composer downloads in a cache under `.composer-cache/` with the fixed key `preflight-proctor`, so repeat runs skip downloads and a lock change fetches only what changed.

The job publishes the report with `artifacts: when: always` as a GitLab Code Quality report (`reports: codequality: gl-code-quality-report.json`), and keeps `proctor.json` in the same artifact (`paths: [proctor.json]`, `expire_in: 30 days`).

### Keep the JSON report for Rollcall [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-proctor.html#keep-the-json-report-for-rollcall)

Goal: Rollcall, the fleet census, shows your app's latest PROCTOR result without anyone copying reports around. With `ROLLCALL_PROCTOR_SOURCE=gitlab`, Rollcall reads `proctor.json` from the artifact of the newest finished `proctor` job on your default branch, passed or failed. That file is PROCTOR's JSON report, the same document `--format=json` prints, written by `proctor check --record` next to the Code Quality output.

Nothing to set: the job does it when your app's PROCTOR is 0.11.0 or later. Before it runs the command, the job checks three things, and adds `--record "$CI_PROJECT_DIR/proctor.json"` only when all hold:

1. `proctor_command` is a plain `proctor check` line: letters, digits, spaces and `/ . _ = : , @ % + -` only. A command with quotes, `$`, `;`, `&&` or a pipe is left as written, so the flag never lands on whatever runs after a shell operator. A `gate` command is left alone too: its `--record` writes a deploy verdict, not the report Rollcall reads.
2. The command does not pass `--record` itself.
3. Your PROCTOR lists `--record` in `proctor check --help` (the job runs the command up to `proctor check`, then `--help`; the rest is left off because Symfony's help has its own `--format` and would refuse `codequality`).

On PROCTOR 0.10.0 or older the job runs exactly as before (those releases exit 2 on an unknown option, so the flag is never sent), the log says no `proctor.json` was kept, and the runner warns `proctor.json: no matching files` while the job keeps its result. Move the app to PROCTOR 0.11.0 or later (`composer require --dev waynestate/proctor:^0.11`, since a `^0.10` constraint stops below 0.11) to start feeding Rollcall.

Note

The guard never changes pass or fail: its `--help` run's exit code is ignored, and the proctor line alone decides the job, as before. When Rollcall reads the job under another name, set `ROLLCALL_PROCTOR_JOB` to your `job_name`.

Tip

A custom command that the guard skips can keep the file on its own: add `--record "$CI_PROJECT_DIR/proctor.json"` to it. The artifact path is the same.

Tip

Set `allow_failure: true` if the job may fail without failing the pipeline; the default is `false`.

### Related [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-proctor.html#related)

- [The php-test component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-php-test.html)
- [The composer-audit component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-composer-audit.html)

---

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-renovate.html

## The renovate component [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-renovate.html#the-renovate-component)

This page covers the `renovate` component: what the job does, how to include it, and every input it takes. Goal: one scheduled job keeps image digests, GitHub action SHAs and package versions current across the group's repositories, and merges the updates whose pipeline is green. The component flies on autopilot; majors keep a human in the seat.

### What the job does [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-renovate.html#what-the-job-does)

The component runs [Renovate](https://docs.renovatebot.com/) as a scheduled or manual job that bumps image digests, GitHub action SHAs and package versions across the group's repositories, and merges the green ones itself. Bumps of `component:` include pins are covered by the preset and wait for review. Majors open a merge request and wait for a person. See [Renovate](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html) for what auto-merges and what waits.

Under the hood, the job:

- Runs only in scheduled pipelines (`$CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "schedule"`) and manual pipelines started from the web (`$CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "web"`).
- Points Renovate at the instance: `RENOVATE_PLATFORM` is `gitlab` and `RENOVATE_ENDPOINT` is `$CI_API_V4_URL`.
- Turns on autodiscovery (`RENOVATE_AUTODISCOVER: "true"`), limited to the `autodiscover_filter` glob, default `$CI_PROJECT_NAMESPACE/*`, relative to the runner project's namespace.
- Writes its `config.js` at job time. The `registryAliases` entry for the GitLab instance comes from the predefined `CI_SERVER_FQDN` variable: GitLab expands the key before the shell runs, and Node resolves the value when Renovate loads `config.js`. No hostname is stored in the template, so the public mirror stays clean.
- Adds the Squire kit commands to the `config.js` `allowedCommands` list when `squire_kit_tasks` is `true`, so the preset's Squire rule can refresh a kit in its merge request (see [Squire kits](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html#squire-kits)). The list is empty otherwise.
- Passes `git_author` through as `RENOVATE_GIT_AUTHOR` and `dry_run` through as `RENOVATE_DRY_RUN`.
- Is interruptible and times out after 1 hour.

Warning

`RENOVATE_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_COM_TOKEN` are not set in the job's `variables:` on purpose. A self-reference such as `RENOVATE_TOKEN: $RENOVATE_TOKEN` arrives as literal text on GitLab 19.5 and shadows the masked project CI/CD variable, so the component leaves both tokens to the project and the masked values reach the job unchanged.

### Include the component [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-renovate.html#include-the-component)

Add the include to the runner project's `.gitlab-ci.yml`, pinned to a full commit SHA with the tag in a trailing comment, and set `git_author`:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/renovate@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
    inputs:
      git_author: "Preflight Bot <preflight-bot@example.com>"
```

### Inputs [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-renovate.html#inputs)

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `job_name` | string | `renovate` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `renovate/renovate:44.192.2@sha256:37960a62ba1faa9079a7c4eead9b3f4470748a64ecd207e06c09fd8858673e17` | Docker image for the job. |
| `image_prefix` | string | `${CI_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GROUP_IMAGE_PREFIX}` | Registry path in front of `image`: the job pulls `image_prefix/image`. The default is the group's GitLab Dependency Proxy, so Docker Hub is asked once and GitLab serves the cached copy. Outside a group with the proxy, set `docker.io`. No trailing slash. |
| `autodiscover_filter` | string | `$CI_PROJECT_NAMESPACE/*` | Glob limiting which projects Renovate discovers, relative to the runner project's namespace. |
| `dry_run` | string | `"null"` | Dry run mode: `null` (disabled), `lookup` or `full`. |
| `git_author` | string | none | Author of the commits and merge requests Renovate creates, in the form `Name <email>`. Required. |
| `squire_kit_tasks` | boolean | `false` | Allow the Squire kit commands of Preflight's preset (install the new `waynestate/squire` from Packagist, then `squire update` on the kit folder), so a Squire kit merge request arrives with its files refreshed. Off, the merge request bumps the version only and shows an artifact error. |

### Verify [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-renovate.html#verify)

Start the job manually from the web, or wait for the schedule. Expected: the job bumps the versions it finds and merges the ones whose pipeline is green. To try it without changes, set `dry_run` to `lookup` or `full`; `null` (disabled) is the default.

### Related [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-renovate.html#related)

- [Renovate](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html): the shared preset, and what auto-merges, what waits and what waits for review.
- [The squire-kit component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-squire-kit.html): the pipeline check that a kit matches the Squire release it records.
- [Include a component twice](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/include-twice.html): the `job_name` input in action.
- [Quick start](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html): wire one component into an app and watch the pipeline run it.
- [Reference](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html): every component, with its inputs and defaults.

## The sbom component [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-sbom.html#the-sbom-component)

This page shows how to add the `sbom` component to an app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`: it generates a CycloneDX SBOM with `cyclonedx/cyclonedx-php-composer`, validates it, and publishes it as an artifact. The SBOM is the aircraft's parts manifest (nothing flies that is not on the list); start with the include, then read what the job does and which inputs it takes.

### Include the component [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-sbom.html#include-the-component)

Add the include to the app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`, pinned to a commit SHA with the tag in a trailing comment:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/sbom@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
    inputs:
      output: sbom.cdx.json
```

A tag or branch can move; a SHA cannot.

### What the job does [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-sbom.html#what-the-job-does)

The job lands in the `test` stage by default, is `interruptible: true`, and has a `timeout: 30 minutes`. It runs four steps:

1. Install the app's dependencies:
   ```sh
   composer install --no-interaction --no-progress --prefer-dist --no-scripts --ignore-platform-reqs
   ```
   The default image is a composer image, which already ships Composer, so no install step for Composer itself is needed. The SBOM lists what the lock installs, so the app's Composer scripts never run here, and the app's PHP version and extensions are not required.
2. Allow the CycloneDX plugin:
   ```sh
   composer global config --no-plugins allow-plugins.cyclonedx/cyclonedx-php-composer true
   ```
3. Install the plugin globally:
   ```sh
   composer global require cyclonedx/cyclonedx-php-composer:^6.2
   ```
   The plugin is installed globally, so the app's `composer.json` is never touched.
4. Generate the SBOM. `--validate` fails the job on an invalid SBOM:
   omit_dev true (default)
   ```sh
   composer CycloneDX:make-sbom --output-format=JSON --output-reproducible --validate --omit=dev --output-file=sbom.cdx.json
   ```
   omit_dev false
   ```sh
   composer CycloneDX:make-sbom --output-format=JSON --output-reproducible --validate --output-file=sbom.cdx.json
   ```
   `--omit=dev` is present only when `omit_dev` is `true`; `--output-file` takes the `output` input (default `sbom.cdx.json`).

### Artifacts [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-sbom.html#artifacts)

The job publishes the SBOM file as an artifact:

```yaml
artifacts:
  paths:
    - sbom.cdx.json
  expire_in: 30 days
```

The path is the `output` input, and the artifact expires in 30 days.

### Inputs [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-sbom.html#inputs)

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `sbom` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `composer:2.11.1@sha256:8de2184c6de224f4689e8f80ed5f5edaf0030b6b8b7839a22a2bcb6722ac87d0` | Docker image for the job. |
| `image_prefix` | string | `${CI_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GROUP_IMAGE_PREFIX}` | Registry path in front of `image`: the job pulls `image_prefix/image`. The default is the group's GitLab Dependency Proxy, so Docker Hub is asked once and GitLab serves the cached copy. Outside a group with the proxy, set `docker.io`. No trailing slash. |
| `omit_dev` | boolean | `true` | Whether to omit dev dependencies from the SBOM. |
| `output` | string | `sbom.cdx.json` | Path of the SBOM file to publish, relative to the project root. It must be a relative path; GitLab refuses the pipeline at creation if it is not. |

`job_name` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$`.

Note

`output` must be a relative path. The input carries a `regex`, so GitLab refuses the pipeline at creation when a value does not match.

### Verify [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-sbom.html#verify)

Push the change. The components are ordinary jobs, so the `sbom` job runs whenever the app's pipeline runs, in the `test` stage by default. A green job means the SBOM was generated, validated, and published.

### Related [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-sbom.html#related)

- [The composer-audit component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-composer-audit.html): the companion dependency check.
- [Include a component twice](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/include-twice.html): the `job_name` input when one project includes the same component more than once.
- [When the components run](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/when-components-run.html): the `workflow:rules` block that belongs in the app's own file.
- [Reference](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html): every component, with its inputs and defaults.
