Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-secret-detection.html

## The secret-detection component [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-secret-detection.html#the-secret-detection-component)

This page covers the `secret-detection` component: what the job does, how to include it, and every input it takes. Goal: a committed secret fails the pipeline before it can ride along in a release. Preflight is named for the pre-flight check, and this component is the row that makes sure nothing classified boards the plane.

Version 1 · Category: Security/Secrets · Tags: security,secrets,gitleaks

### What the job does [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-secret-detection.html#what-the-job-does)

The component runs [Gitleaks](https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks) over the checked-out tree and fails the pipeline when a rule matches. By default it runs Gitleaks' built-in rules plus a path allowlist for `vendor/` and `node_modules/`: Gitleaks scans whatever is checked out, and a CI cache can restore either tree, so their findings are not our code. Point `config_path` at your own `.gitleaks.toml` to replace the default, and add the same `vendor` and `node_modules` path allowlist to your file. Every match is redacted: the job log and the report carry the rule, the file and the line, never the value.

The job, in order:

1. Writes the default config to `/tmp` (outside the scanned tree) unless `config_path` is set, then runs `gitleaks dir` over the project root with `--redact` and `--config`, writing a JSON report to `gitleaks.json` at the project root.
2. Exits with Gitleaks' exit code: 0 when the tree is clean, 1 when a rule matched.

The report is published as an artifact even when the job fails, so a red pipeline still shows what was found (redacted). The job is interruptible and times out after 30 minutes.

### Include the component [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-secret-detection.html#include-the-component)

Add the include to the app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`, pinned to the full commit SHA of the release that first ships the component, with the tag in a trailing comment:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/secret-detection@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
```

### Inputs [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-secret-detection.html#inputs)

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `secret-detection` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `zricethezav/gitleaks:v8.30.1@sha256:c00b6bd0aeb3071cbcb79009cb16a60dd9e0a7c60e2be9ab65d25e6bc8abbb7f` | Docker image for the job. |
| `image_prefix` | string | `${CI_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GROUP_IMAGE_PREFIX}` | Registry path in front of `image`: the job pulls `image_prefix/image`. The default is the group's GitLab Dependency Proxy, so Docker Hub is asked once and GitLab serves the cached copy. Outside a group with the proxy, set `docker.io`. No trailing slash. |
| `config_path` | string | (empty) | Path to a `.gitleaks.toml` config file, relative to the project root. Empty uses the built-in rules plus a path allowlist for `vendor/` and `node_modules/`. When set, your file replaces the default, so add the same `vendor` and `node_modules` path allowlist to it. |
| `allow_failure` | boolean | `false` | Whether the job can fail without failing the pipeline. |

### Allowlist a false positive [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-secret-detection.html#allowlist-a-false-positive)

Two ways, both reviewed like code:

- **`.gitleaksignore`** at the project root: one fingerprint per line, in the form `file:rule:line`. Copy the fingerprint from the job log or the `gitleaks.json` artifact. In `dir` mode Gitleaks reads the file without an extra flag.
- **A config file**: commit a `.gitleaks.toml` (start from Gitleaks' default config and add your own rules and allowlists) and set `config_path` to it. Your file replaces the job's default, so it must carry the same path allowlist for the dependency trees:
  ```toml
  [allowlist]
  description = "skip dependency trees: vendor and node_modules are not our code"
  paths = ['''(^|/)vendor/''', '''(^|/)node_modules/''']
  ```

Note

While the stack rolls the component out, `allow_failure: true` keeps the pipeline green while a team clears its backlog. The default is `false`: once the tree is clean, a new secret fails the pipeline.

### Verify [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-secret-detection.html#verify)

Push the change. The `secret-detection` job lands in the `test` stage by default, and a green job means Gitleaks found nothing in the tree.

### Related [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-secret-detection.html#related)

- [Quick start](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html): wire one component into an app and watch the pipeline run it.
- [Install](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html): the requirements, the include snippet, and how to verify.
- [Include a component twice](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/include-twice.html): the `job_name` input in action.
- [Reference](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html): every component, with its inputs and defaults.

---

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-squire-kit.html

## The squire-kit component [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-squire-kit.html#the-squire-kit-component)

This page covers the `squire-kit` component: what the job checks, how to include it, every input it takes, and what to do when it goes red. Goal: a deploy kit that [Squire](https://github.com/waynestate/squire) wrote stays exactly what Squire wrote, so a fix to the kit reaches every app the day Squire ships it. A squire keeps the armor polished; this job is the inspection before the joust.

Version 1 · Category: Testing/Validation · Tags: squire,deploy,drift

### What the job checks [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-squire-kit.html#what-the-job-checks)

Squire writes the deploy kit (`build.sh`, the release script, the health check, the local parity files) and records the Squire version it used and a SHA-256 of every file in `.squire.json`. The job:

1. Moves to the kit folder given by `working_dir` (the stack's own repos keep the kit in `deploy`).
2. Reads the version recorded in `.squire.json`, unless `squire_version` names one.
3. Installs that exact Squire release from Packagist into a temporary folder outside the project, with `--no-dev` and `--no-scripts`, so nothing from the project and none of Squire's dev tools run.
4. Runs `squire init --check` on the kit folder.

It passes only when every kit file is that release's template, untouched. The exit codes are Squire's:

| Exit | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | The kit matches the recorded release. |
| 1 | The kit drifted: a file was edited (`modified`), is missing, is not the template of the recorded release (`outdated`), or is new in the kit's groups (`untracked`). |
| 2 | The check could not run: no `.squire.json` in `working_dir`, no released `x.y.z` version recorded, or no such release on Packagist. |

The job checks the version the kit records, not the newest Squire, so a new Squire release never turns a green main red by itself. Renovate moves the version: the [Renovate](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html) preset opens a merge request for each new Squire, and on a runner that allows it, that merge request already carries the refreshed kit.

### Include the component [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-squire-kit.html#include-the-component)

Add the include to the app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`, pinned to a full commit SHA with the tag in a trailing comment:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/squire-kit@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
    inputs:
      working_dir: deploy
```

Note

The squire-kit component ships in Preflight 0.2.0; 0.1.4 does not include it. Pin that tag's full commit SHA, or the full commit SHA of a commit at or after it.

Run `vendor/bin/squire init --check --path=deploy` on your desk first. Include the component once it passes, or turn on `allow_failure` while you clean up (below).

### Inputs [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-squire-kit.html#inputs)

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `squire-kit` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `composer:2.11.1@sha256:8de2184c6de224f4689e8f80ed5f5edaf0030b6b8b7839a22a2bcb6722ac87d0` | Docker image for the job. It needs PHP 8.3 or later and Composer. |
| `image_prefix` | string | `${CI_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GROUP_IMAGE_PREFIX}` | Registry path in front of `image`: the job pulls `image_prefix/image`. The default is the group's GitLab Dependency Proxy, so Docker Hub is asked once and GitLab serves the cached copy. Outside a group with the proxy, set `docker.io`. No trailing slash. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | The kit folder: the one holding `.squire.json`, relative to the project root. |
| `squire_version` | string | `""` | Squire release to check against. Empty reads the version recorded in `.squire.json`. |
| `allow_failure` | boolean | `false` | Whether the job can fail without failing the pipeline, for a repository cleaning up its first findings. |

`job_name` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$`, `working_dir` must match `^(\.|[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9._/-]*)$`, and `squire_version` must be empty or match `^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$`. GitLab refuses the pipeline at creation when a value does not match.

### When the job is red [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-squire-kit.html#when-the-job-is-red)

The log lists every kit file with its state; the last lines name what to do.

- **`outdated` or `missing`.** The kit records a version whose templates it does not carry. Run `vendor/bin/squire update --path=deploy`, then `vendor/bin/squire init --path=deploy` (a release that adds a kit file needs `init` to write it), review the diff and commit it.
- **`modified`.** Someone, or a bot, edited a file Squire owns. Put Squire's file back with `vendor/bin/squire init --force --path=deploy` and send the change to Squire instead, so every app gets it.
- **`untracked`.** A file sits in one of the kit's groups but not in `.squire.json`. Remove it, or run `squire init` so Squire records it.

> \[!CAUTION\] Renovate's digest and tag bumps were what made the stack's kits drift: a bump to a base image inside `.squire/` or to `docker-compose.squire.yml` is an edit to a file Squire owns. Preflight's preset now leaves those files alone; update the image in Squire's templates and let the next Squire release carry it.

### Adopt it with findings [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-squire-kit.html#adopt-it-with-findings)

To include the component before the kit is clean, let the job fail without failing the pipeline:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/squire-kit@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
    inputs:
      working_dir: deploy
      allow_failure: true # until 2026-12-01: kit cleanup
```

While `allow_failure` is `true`, a red job shows as a warning. Remove the input once the job is green, and leave a date in a comment so the warning does not become the new normal.

### Verify [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-squire-kit.html#verify)

Push the change. The `squire-kit` job lands in the `test` stage by default and its last line reads `RESULT: pass (0 of N files need attention)` when the kit matches. Preflight's own pipeline runs it on `tests/squire-kit-fixture`, a kit written by `squire init --target=raw`.

Note

The job needs Packagist (to install the recorded Squire release). It needs no token and no Docker socket.

### Related [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-squire-kit.html#related)

- [Renovate](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html): the preset's Squire rule, which opens the merge request that moves the kit to a new release.
- [The renovate component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-renovate.html): the `squire_kit_tasks` input, which lets that merge request carry the refreshed kit.
- [Include a component twice](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/include-twice.html): check two kits in one project with `job_name`.
- [Troubleshooting](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html): the squire-kit job's error messages.
- [Reference](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html): every component, with its inputs and defaults.

---

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/dependency-caching.html

## Dependency caching [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/dependency-caching.html#dependency-caching)

Every image and package a pipeline downloads is a request to someone else's server. Docker Hub limits anonymous pulls per address, and a runner that starts fifty jobs on a busy afternoon can hit that limit, or worse, look like abuse. This page covers how the components keep those downloads cached: images through GitLab's Dependency Proxy, Composer and npm packages in the GitLab cache. Read how the image prefix works, what to set on a GitLab without the proxy, and how the check keeps it that way. A preflight check is cheapest when it finds nothing; a cache is cheapest when nobody notices it.

### Images: the image_prefix input [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/dependency-caching.html#images-the-image-prefix-input)

Each component whose image comes from Docker Hub (`proctor`, `php-test`, `composer-audit`, `sbom`, `pint`, `phpstan`, `eslint`, `secret-detection`, `package-publish`, `renovate` and `squire-kit`) has an `image_prefix` input. The job pulls `image_prefix/image`:

| Input | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `image_prefix` | `${CI_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GROUP_IMAGE_PREFIX}` |
| `image` | the component's image, for example `composer:2.11.1@sha256:...` |

`CI_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GROUP_IMAGE_PREFIX` is the top-level group's [Dependency Proxy](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/packages/dependency_proxy/). The runner signs in to it on its own, the proxy asks Docker Hub once, and every later pull of the same digest is served from GitLab. Digest pins still hold: the proxy serves the exact image the digest names.

`image` is the path after the prefix. Set it to change the image, not the registry:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/proctor@<sha> # <version>
    inputs:
      image: php:8.5-cli-trixie@sha256:<digest>
```

#### On a GitLab or group without the proxy [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/dependency-caching.html#on-a-gitlab-or-group-without-the-proxy)

Set `image_prefix` to Docker Hub itself:

```yaml
    inputs:
      image_prefix: docker.io
```

`docker.io` works for every Docker Hub image. `docker.io/library` also works for the official images (`php`, `composer`, `node`) but not for `renovate/renovate` or `zricethezav/gitleaks`. For another registry, put its host and path in `image_prefix` and the rest in `image`, for example `image_prefix: registry.example.com/mirror` with `image: php:8.4-cli-trixie@sha256:<digest>`. The prefix has no trailing slash; the input's pattern refuses one.

#### Upgrading from a version without image_prefix [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/dependency-caching.html#upgrading-from-a-version-without-image-prefix)

Apps that passed `image: ${CI_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GROUP_IMAGE_PREFIX}/...` only to reach the proxy drop that input when they move to this version: the default now does it, and keeping it would put the prefix in twice.

#### Images the proxy cannot serve [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/dependency-caching.html#images-the-proxy-cannot-serve)

The Dependency Proxy serves Docker Hub only. The `a11y` component's Playwright image (`mcr.microsoft.com`) and the `portability` component's Buildah image (`quay.io`) are pulled from their own registries and have no `image_prefix`; the runner's own image cache is what saves those pulls.

### Packages: the cache blocks [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/dependency-caching.html#packages-the-cache-blocks)

Each job that installs packages keeps them in the GitLab cache, inside the project so GitLab can save and restore them:

| Component | Path | Key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `php-test` | `.composer-cache/` | fixed per PHP version (`preflight-php-${PHP_VERSION}`) |
| `proctor`, `pint`, `phpstan`, `sbom` | `.composer-cache/` | fixed (`preflight-proctor`, `preflight-pint`, `preflight-phpstan`, `preflight-sbom`) |
| `squire-kit` | `.composer-cache/` | fixed (`preflight-squire-kit`), unchanged |
| `eslint` | `.npm-cache/` | fixed (`preflight-eslint`) |
| `a11y` | `.npm-cache/` | fixed (`preflight-a11y`), unchanged |

`npm-audit` installs nothing, so it keeps no cache of its own. It reads the app's npm cache instead: key `npm`, path `.cache/npm/` (`npm_config_cache`), the ones Sourdough's generated pipelines use, with `policy: pull`, so an audit next to the app's install job never overwrites what that job downloaded.

`COMPOSER_CACHE_DIR` and `NPM_CONFIG_CACHE` point the tools at those paths. The keys are fixed and installs still resolve from the lock, so a cached run never installs a stale package: Composer and npm only skip the download. Every component cache also saves with `when: always`, so a retry after a dropped download fetches only what is missing.

### Your own jobs [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/dependency-caching.html#your-own-jobs)

The same pattern fits an app's own jobs, such as `composer-ci` or a front-end build. Sourdough's app templates ship it:

```yaml
variables:
  IMAGE_PREFIX: "${CI_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GROUP_IMAGE_PREFIX}"
  COMPOSER_CACHE_DIR: "$CI_PROJECT_DIR/.cache/composer"

composer-ci:
  image: ${IMAGE_PREFIX}/composer:2.11.1
  cache:
    key: composer
    paths: [.cache/composer/]
    when: always
  script:
    - composer install --no-interaction --no-progress --prefer-dist
    - composer ci
```

### How it stays that way [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/dependency-caching.html#how-it-stays-that-way)

`tests/check-dependency-cache.sh` (and its `.ps1` twin) runs in Preflight's `contract` job and fails when:

- a component's image default is on Docker Hub but the component has no `image_prefix` input defaulting to the proxy, or a job image skips it;
- a component runs `composer install`, `update`, `require` or `create-project`, or `npm ci` or `install`, without a `cache:` block and a cache directory;
- Preflight's own `.gitlab-ci.yml` pulls a Docker Hub image without the proxy prefix, or passes a component an image that already carries it.

### Related [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/dependency-caching.html#related)

- [Updating image pins](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/image-pins.html): how the digests behind `image` are chosen and changed.
- [The php-test component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-php-test.html): the matrix and its per-version cache.
- [GitLab: Dependency Proxy](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/packages/dependency_proxy/) and [GitLab: caching](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/caching/).

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/deprecation.html

## Deprecating and removing a component [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/deprecation.html#deprecating-and-removing-a-component)

Apps pin Preflight by tag, so a removal is only fair when it was announced first. This page is the policy: what never changes, what may go and in which release, how the announcement works, and how to find out who still pins a version before anything is removed. A deprecation notice is the preflight checklist for goodbye: read it twice, then take off.

### What never changes [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/deprecation.html#what-never-changes)

- Published tags are never moved or deleted. An app that pins `component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/<name>@<version>` keeps resolving that reference, and its pipeline keeps running, for as long as the app wants it.
- A deprecation is a promise with a date, not a mood. The notice names the replacement and the release that removes it, and both parts of the promise must hold.

### What may go, and in which release [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/deprecation.html#what-may-go-and-in-which-release)

An input, a job name or a default that an app may rely on is removed only in a minor release while Preflight is below 1.0, or in a major release after 1.0. The CHANGELOG entry for the removal says what replaces it, so an app that reads the changelog knows where to move.

### How the deprecation is announced [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/deprecation.html#how-the-deprecation-is-announced)

Deprecation comes first, one full release ahead of removal:

- The CHANGELOG gets a `Deprecated:` bullet naming the input, job or component and its replacement.
- The component's guide gets a note at the top of the page naming the replacement and the release that removes it.
- Where the component can, its job log prints one line saying it is deprecated, so the app sees the notice in every pipeline run.

A whole component stays in the repo and in the Catalog for at least 6 months after its deprecation release, even if nobody has pinned it since.

### The Catalog toggle stays on [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/deprecation.html#the-catalog-toggle-stays-on)

The CI/CD Catalog toggle is never turned off while any published version is still pinned somewhere in the group. Turning it off deletes the Catalog metadata for every published version ([GitLab: components, unpublishing](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/components/)), and republishing needs a new release. Whether `component:` includes pinned by SHA keep working afterwards is unverified, so do not rely on it.

To find who still pins a version, search the group for `preflight/<name>@`. Rollcall lists the apps that carry the pin, so the fleet report agrees with the search before the toggle question is even asked.

### Related [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/deprecation.html#related)

- [Upgrading](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html)
- [What the components cannot force](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-components-cannot-force.html)
- [GitLab: CI/CD components](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/components/)

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/github-mirrors.html

## GitHub mirrors [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/github-mirrors.html#github-mirrors)

Preflight's components fly inside one GitLab instance only, so this page shows how a package that is also mirrored to `github.com/waynestate` still gets the same checks: call Preflight's reusable GitHub Actions workflow from the mirror's own `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Start here, then read [Same instance only](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/same-instance-only.html) for why the components cannot cross instances.

### Why the mirror needs its own workflow [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/github-mirrors.html#why-the-mirror-needs-its-own-workflow)

Components work only inside one GitLab instance, so a package that is also mirrored to `github.com/waynestate` cannot include them there. For those mirrors, Preflight ships a reusable GitHub Actions workflow that runs the same checks: the package's `composer ci` script on each supported PHP version, plus a Composer audit.

### The workflow just calls `composer ci` [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/github-mirrors.html#the-workflow-just-calls-composer-ci)

Each package keeps its checks in a `ci` script in its `composer.json`; the workflow just calls `composer ci`, so the mirror runs whatever the package already runs on GitLab.

### Call the workflow from your package [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/github-mirrors.html#call-the-workflow-from-your-package)

The workflow lives at `.github/workflows/php-package.yml` in this repo. A mirrored package calls it from its own `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:

```yaml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: ['**']
    tags: ['v*', '*.*.*']

jobs:
  ci:
    uses: waynestate/preflight/.github/workflows/php-package.yml@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
```

### Pin the include to a commit SHA [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/github-mirrors.html#pin-the-include-to-a-commit-sha)

This workflow ships in the `0.1.1` tag, so pin the full commit SHA of the release tag and keep the tag in a trailing comment. A tag or branch can move; a SHA cannot. PROCTOR's `preflight-pinned` check warns when an include is not pinned to a commit SHA. The Renovate preset (see the Renovate section) proposes the bumps, and they wait for review (the `needs-review` label).

### Workflow inputs [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/github-mirrors.html#workflow-inputs)

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `php-versions` | string (JSON array) | `'["8.3","8.4","8.5"]'` | PHP versions to test, lowest first. The audit job runs on the first entry. |
| `ci-command` | string | `composer ci` | The command to run in each PHP version job. |
| `working-directory` | string | `.` | Directory to run the command in, relative to the repository root. |

### Green on both sides [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/github-mirrors.html#green-on-both-sides)

The workflow is committed to this repo (and so to GitLab) but only runs on the GitHub mirror; GitLab ignores `.github/workflows`. A release tag is not done until it is green on both sides. Two cockpits, one checklist.

### Related [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/github-mirrors.html#related)

- [Same instance only](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/same-instance-only.html)
- [Renovate](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html)
- [Composer audit component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-composer-audit.html)

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/image-pins.html

## Updating image pins [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/image-pins.html#updating-image-pins)

This page covers the image pins Preflight's components run: why they are digests, how to look one up, and how to change one. Read the pinning rules, look up the new digest, and open a reviewed merge request. Like the aircraft preflight it is named after, the value shows up on the day it catches something.

### Why pins are digests [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/image-pins.html#why-pins-are-digests)

Every image the components run is pinned by digest (`name:tag@sha256:...`), so a repointed tag cannot quietly change what a pipeline executes. The tag stays in front of the digest so a diff still reads like a version bump.

Note

The php-test matrix is the one exception. Its PHP images are tag-pinned on purpose, so those jobs run on the newest PHP patch release; every other component image is digest-pinned.

### Look up the digest [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/image-pins.html#look-up-the-digest)

To look up the digest for an image:

```sh
docker buildx imagetools inspect <image>:<tag>
```

Use the top-level `Digest:` line (the multi-arch index digest), not a per-platform one. Without `buildx`, `docker manifest inspect -v <image>:<tag>` shows the same index digest.

### Change a pin [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/image-pins.html#change-a-pin)

Pins change only through a reviewed merge request.

### Related [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/image-pins.html#related)

- [Dependency caching](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/dependency-caching.html): the `image_prefix` input in front of each pin, and the package caches.
- [Template lint](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/template-lint.html): the unsafe CI patterns `composer ci` scans for before the fixture tests.
- [Shared conventions](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/conventions.html): Composer vendor, license, PHP floor and JavaScript installs.

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/include-twice.html

## Include a component twice [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/include-twice.html#include-a-component-twice)

Goal: run the same component more than once in one project, for example in a monorepo with two apps, and keep the two jobs separate. Set the `job_name` input on each include, as shown below.

### Set `job_name` [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/include-twice.html#set-job-name)

Every component takes a `job_name` input, whose default is the job's usual name. Set it when one project includes the same component more than once, for example in a monorepo with two apps; without it the two jobs would share a name and merge into one.

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/pint@<full commit SHA> # <tag>
    inputs:
      working_dir: app
      job_name: pint-app
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/pint@<full commit SHA> # <tag>
    inputs:
      working_dir: admin
      job_name: pint-admin
```

Expected: the pipeline runs two separately named jobs, `pint-app` and `pint-admin`, instead of two jobs that merge into one.

Note

`job_name` ships in 0.1.4, so pin 0.1.4 or a SHA at or after that release. `portability` gained it with its one-job form, in 0.2.0.

### Another use: the next PHP release [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/include-twice.html#another-use-the-next-php-release)

Including a component twice is also how you try a PHP release before it is supported. Include `php-test` a second time for the release that is not supported yet, name that job, and let it fail. The name is what lets your own `.gitlab-ci.yml` loosen only that job:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@<full commit SHA> # <tag>
    inputs:
      php_versions: ["8.6"]
      job_name: php-test-next
      # While 8.6 only has release candidate images, name the tag: php:${PHP_VERSION}-rc-cli-trixie
      # image: "php:${PHP_VERSION}-rc-cli-trixie"

php-test-next:
  allow_failure: true
```

A red `php-test-next` job is an early warning, not a stop. Drop the `allow_failure` and move the version into the main `php_versions` list once the release is supported (the supported versions follow `policy.json`).

### Related [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/include-twice.html#related)

- [The php-test component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-php-test.html): inputs, caching, and the full next-release example.
- [The portability component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-portability.html): include it once per app image, each with its own `job_name`.
- [When the components run](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/when-components-run.html): the `workflow:rules` block that belongs in the app's own file.
- [Reference](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html): every component, with its inputs and defaults.

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/inputs-contract.html

## The inputs contract [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/inputs-contract.html#the-inputs-contract)

Your app's `include:` lines lean on names: `php_versions`, `working_dir`, a job called `php-test` that your own `.gitlab-ci.yml` may extend. This page says what Preflight promises about those names, where the promise is written down, and how to read what changed before you move a pin. A pilot reads the weight and balance sheet before takeoff, not after the wheels leave the runway.

### What the contract holds [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/inputs-contract.html#what-the-contract-holds)

[`contract/inputs.json`](https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/preflight/-/blob/main/contract/inputs.json) lists every component in `templates/`, and for each one:

- every input, in template order, with its `type`, its `default` (when it has one) and its `regex` (when the template limits the value);
- every job the component adds, by name (php-test adds `php-test`, and `php-test-advisory` when `php_advisory_version` is set).

An entry looks like this (php-test, abridged):

```json
"php-test": {
  "inputs": [
    { "name": "php_versions", "type": "array", "default": ["8.3", "8.4", "8.5"] },
    { "name": "php_advisory_version", "type": "string", "default": "", "regex": "^$|^[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+([.][0-9A-Za-z]+)*$" },
    { "name": "test_command", "type": "string", "default": "vendor/bin/phpunit" },
    { "name": "working_dir", "type": "string", "default": ".", "regex": "^(\\.|[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9._/-]*)$" }
  ],
  "jobs": ["php-test", "php-test-advisory"]
}
```

### How Preflight holds itself to it [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/inputs-contract.html#how-preflight-holds-itself-to-it)

The templates cannot drift from the file. Two checks compare them on every Preflight pipeline:

- `tests/ComponentsContractTest.php`, a PHPUnit suite that `composer ci` runs. It parses every template and fails on any difference, naming the component and the input or job that was added, removed or changed, and it says that a rename is a breaking change.
- `tests/check-contract.sh` and its `.ps1` twin, in the `contract` job, which make the same comparison and also reject any top-level key in a template that is not one of its jobs (no `default:`, `variables:` or `workflow:` leaking into your pipeline).

When a change to the surface is made on purpose, the same commit rewrites the file with `composer contract:update`, so the change shows up in review as a diff of `contract/inputs.json`, not as a surprise in your pipeline.

### What that means for your pin [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/inputs-contract.html#what-that-means-for-your-pin)

- **Renames and removals are announced.** An input or job is renamed or removed only in a release whose section in [Upgrading](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html) lists it under Breaking. Before 1.0, Preflight treats the minor number as the major one: breaking changes land in a new minor (0.3 to 0.4), and a patch (0.3.0 to 0.3.1) keeps every input, default and job name.
- **A tighter `regex` counts as breaking.** A value your include used to pass can stop passing; 0.4.0's Composer floor on `composer_version` is the example, and its Upgrading section says so.
- **Defaults move, in the open.** Pinned image digests are defaults too, and Renovate moves them between releases. If your include leaves an input unset, you get the new default when you move the pin; the contract diff shows each one.
- **Your own job overrides keep working** as long as the job name is in the contract. Overriding a job by a name that is not there (an internal helper, a hidden `.key`) is not covered.

### See what moved between two tags [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/inputs-contract.html#see-what-moved-between-two-tags)

From a clone of Preflight, diff the contract between the tag you pin and the one you are moving to:

```
git diff 0.4.0 0.5.0 -- contract/inputs.json
```

From 0.4.0 to 0.5.0 that shows the new `npm-audit` entry, the `composer_version` default on php-test and proctor moving from 2.10.3 to 2.11.1, and every Composer `image` default moving to `composer:2.11.1`: one new component and defaults that moved in the open, nothing renamed or removed. It also shows the renovate `dry_run` pattern, which the template already enforced in 0.4.0 and the contract now records. From 0.3.1 to 0.4.0 the same command shows proctor's new `git_depth` input, php-test's `php_advisory_version` input and its `php-test-advisory` job, and the Composer floor (`regex`) on both components' `composer_version`. Every line of that diff should have a matching line in the version's Upgrading section; if one does not, open an issue.

### Related [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/inputs-contract.html#related)

- [Upgrading](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html): what each release changed, and the steps to move a pin.
- [Components](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html): every component, with its inputs and defaults.
- [Include a component twice](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/include-twice.html): the `job_name` input every component takes.
- [Local checks](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/local-checks.html): `composer test`, `composer contract:update` and the rest of the scripts.

## Strongly recommended: a git.wayne.edu instance runner [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/instance-runner.html#strongly-recommended-a-git-wayne-edu-instance-runner)

This page explains why a git.wayne.edu instance runner is still strongly recommended and exactly what to ask for when you request one. Read it before you file the request, and carry the three asks below into the request itself.

### Why the recommendation exists [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/instance-runner.html#why-the-recommendation-exists)

git.wayne.edu now has an instance runner, and the stack's CI runs on it. Every product in the stack still strongly recommends a git.wayne.edu instance runner, so that capacity stays there.

### What to ask for [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/instance-runner.html#what-to-ask-for)

Ask for:

- A non-privileged Docker executor (no privileged mode, no Docker socket mount).
- A fresh ephemeral environment for every job.
- No shell executor shared between projects.

Capacity and maintenance stay with ops.

Tip

A job that needs the host's Docker socket to take off has skipped its own preflight.

- [Same instance only](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/same-instance-only.html)

## Keep the job token allowlist short [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/job-token-allowlist.html#keep-the-job-token-allowlist-short)

This page is for an app that installs private packages from GitLab's package registry. It sets out what belongs in the CI/CD job token allowlist, where the setting lives, and when to review it. Apply the rule once, then repeat the review whenever a dependency is dropped.

### What to list [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/job-token-allowlist.html#what-to-list)

An app that installs private packages from GitLab's package registry should list only the projects it really needs in its CI/CD job token allowlist (project settings, Settings, CI/CD, Job token permissions), use the fine-grained permissions where they fit, and review the list when a dependency is dropped.

Warning

A leaked job token acts with the triggering user's access.

### When to review [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/job-token-allowlist.html#when-to-review)

Review the list when a dependency is dropped, and drop any project the app no longer installs from it.

### What Preflight cannot do [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/job-token-allowlist.html#what-preflight-cannot-do)

This is a project setting, not a file Preflight can create or check. The setting is made in the app's GitLab project settings, so no file in the app's repository sets it for you.

### Related [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/job-token-allowlist.html#related)

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html

## Quick start [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#quick-start)

This quick start adds the `php-test` component to an app, the same way the front page shows it. Every other component installs the same way: one include, pinned to a commit SHA.

1. **Check the requirements.** Your GitLab must be 17.0 or newer (components are GA on the Free tier since GitLab 17.0), and the app must live on the same GitLab instance that hosts this project. Expected: both true, or the components cannot run here.
2. **Add the include** to the app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`:
   ```yaml
   include:
     - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
     inputs:
       test_command: vendor/bin/phpunit
   ```
   Expected: the file includes the component pinned to a full commit SHA, with the tag in a trailing comment. A tag or branch can move; a SHA cannot.
3. **Commit and push** the change:
   ```sh
   git push
   ```
   Expected: the next pipeline runs the `php-test` jobs, one per entry of `php_versions`, `8.3`, `8.4` and `8.5` by default, each in the `test` stage.
4. **Read the result.** Each job installs the app's dependencies, caches Composer downloads in `.composer-cache/`, and runs the test command. Expected: a green matrix, meaning the app passes on every supported PHP version.

### What you built [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#what-you-built)

Your app now runs the same PHP tests on each supported PHP version that every WSU app runs, from one pinned include. Add the remaining components the same way, one include each.

### Next steps [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#next-steps)

- [Install](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html): requirements, the full include, and how to verify.
- [When the components run](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/when-components-run.html): the `workflow:rules` block that keeps the checks on merge requests and the default branch.
- [The php-test component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-php-test.html): inputs, caching, and trying the next PHP release without breaking the pipeline.
- [Reference](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html): every component, with its inputs and defaults.

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html

## Renovate: what merges and what waits [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html#renovate-what-merges-and-what-waits)

This page covers what Preflight's version automation auto-merges, what waits for a person, and how the private runner project is set up. For the component's inputs, go to [the `renovate` component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-renovate.html).

### How it works [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html#how-it-works)

Preflight owns the stack's version automation (ADR-0015): the shared preset `renovate/default.json` and the [`renovate` component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-renovate.html) that runs it. A private runner project includes the component on a schedule; Renovate discovers every repository in the filter, opens merge requests for outdated versions, and GitLab's native auto-merge takes in the ones whose pipeline is green.

Every stack repository carries a `renovate.json` that extends the shared preset, so the rules change in one place:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://docs.renovatebot.com/renovate-schema.json",
  "extends": ["local>enterprise-apps/preflight//renovate/default"]
}
```

### What auto-merges [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html#what-auto-merges)

Digest updates, pin and pinDigest updates, and patch and minor version bumps auto-merge when the pipeline is green. Lock file maintenance runs weekly and auto-merges the same way. Every merge request carries the `auto-deps` label.

The exception is Preflight's own pins: an update that touches the templates, the contract or this repository's own pipeline, a bump of a component include version, and a bump of the recorded Squire kit version, never auto-merge (see [What waits for review](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html#what-waits-for-review)).

### What waits [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html#what-waits)

Major version bumps never auto-merge. The merge request carries the `major` label and waits for a person.

### What waits for review [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html#what-waits-for-review)

Updates that change an image digest inside the templates, the contract, or this repository's own pipeline, bumps of a Preflight component version in an app's `component:` include, and bumps of the recorded Squire kit version (labeled `squire-kit`) carry the `needs-review` label and never auto-merge. They wait for a person because those pins are what every app pipeline runs: a changed digest here changes what every consuming pipeline executes, so it earns a human eye even when its own pipeline is green. The Squire kit version bump also changes the kit's files; see [Squire kits](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html#squire-kits).

### Squire kits [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html#squire-kits)

A Squire deploy kit (the `deploy` folder in the stack's repos) is files Squire wrote, recorded with their hashes in `deploy/.squire.json`. Two rules in the preset keep it equal to a Squire release:

- **A new Squire refreshes the kit.** The custom manager reads the version in `.squire.json` and opens a merge request for each new `waynestate/squire` on Packagist. Its `postUpgradeTasks` install that release into a folder under `/tmp` (outside the repository, `--no-dev --no-scripts`) and run `squire update` on the kit folder, so the merge request carries the refreshed files. It waits for review (`squire-kit`, `needs-review`).
- **Renovate leaves kit files alone.** Updates to `docker-compose.squire.yml` and anything under `.squire/` are turned off outside Squire's own `templates/` folders. A digest or tag bump there is an edit to a file Squire owns: the kit drifts from its release, and the next `squire update` refuses to overwrite it. Change the image in Squire's templates instead; the next Squire release carries it to every kit.

Renovate only runs a post-upgrade command its runner allows. The [`renovate` component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-renovate.html)'s `squire_kit_tasks` input (default `false`) writes the allow-list into the runner's `config.js`: two anchored patterns that match the exact `composer create-project` and `squire update` commands, with the version and paths limited to safe characters. No shell runs the commands. Without the input, the merge request bumps the version only and shows an artifact error; refresh it by hand with `vendor/bin/squire update --path=deploy`, review the diff and commit it to the branch.

A Squire release that adds a kit file needs `vendor/bin/squire init --path=deploy` as well: `squire update` refreshes the files the kit already lists and does not write new ones. The [`squire-kit` component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-squire-kit.html) catches both cases, and any hand edit, by running `squire init --check` in the pipeline.

### Why MySQL and HA-Proxy get digests only [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html#why-mysql-and-ha-proxy-get-digests-only)

The `mysql` and `haproxy` images mirror the versions Citadel actually runs, not the newest releases in the world. Bumping their tags would drift the apps away from production, so only digest updates are enabled for them: the same tag, the exact image. `citadel/php-apache` is disabled entirely, because Squire's own data owns that image.

### Pinned to immutable tags [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html#pinned-to-immutable-tags)

The `quay.io/buildah/stable` image (the `image` default of the portability component) is matched to `-immutable` tags only. Red Hat re-pushed v1.43.5 under the mutable tag and garbage-collected the old digest, which broke an image job, so Drawbridge and Squire now pin the immutable form, `v1.43.5-immutable@sha256:...`. The preset carries a packageRule for `quay.io/buildah/stable` with a regex versioning that only matches `vX.Y.Z-immutable` tags, so Renovate proposes updates within the immutable tags and never moves a pin back to a mutable one. Digests stay pinned as before (`docker:pinDigests`).

### Set up (the user does this) [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html#set-up-the-user-does-this)

This repository ships the preset and the component, and creates nothing else. A person must set up:

- A private runner project that includes the `renovate` component on a schedule (see [The runner project](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html#the-runner-project)).
- The `RENOVATE_TOKEN` masked CI variable in that project, and optionally `GITHUB_COM_TOKEN`.
- A pipeline schedule on that project so the job runs regularly; weekly on Monday is a sensible default.
- To let Squire kit merge requests arrive refreshed, `squire_kit_tasks: true` under the include's `inputs:`, on a Preflight version that has the input (see [Squire kits](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html#squire-kits)).

### The runner project [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html#the-runner-project)

Warning

The runner project must stay private. It holds `RENOVATE_TOKEN`, a token that can open and merge merge requests across the group, and this repository is mirrored to public GitHub. Use a group bot account for the token, not a person's: the bot outlives any one maintainer, and the commits keep one stable author.

| Variable | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `RENOVATE_TOKEN` | yes | Masked CI variable in the runner project; the job reads it straight from the project, the component does not map it. A project access token with Developer, or Maintainer where only Maintainers may merge. |
| `GITHUB_COM_TOKEN` | no | Masked CI variable in the runner project; the job reads it straight from the project, the component does not map it. Lookups against github.com do not hit anonymous rate limits. |

Warning

Do not add `RENOVATE_TOKEN: $RENOVATE_TOKEN` to your own `variables:`; that self-reference arrives as literal text.

The component writes its `config.js` at job time, so the `registryAliases` entry for the GitLab instance comes from the predefined `CI_SERVER_FQDN` variable. No hostname is stored in this repository.

### Related [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html#related)

- [The `renovate` component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-renovate.html)
- [The `squire-kit` component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-squire-kit.html)

## Same instance only [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/same-instance-only.html#same-instance-only)

This page tells you where Preflight components can run, and what to do when your app is not on the right instance. Read it before you add an include if your app lives on a different GitLab than this project.

### The rule [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/same-instance-only.html#the-rule)

Components work only inside the GitLab instance that hosts this project.

Warning

Components cannot be used across instances except by mirroring.

Every include in this manual takes the form `component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/<name>@<full commit SHA>`. The path is built from `$CI_SERVER_FQDN`, the instance the pipeline runs on, so the component must be resolvable on that same instance.

### What that means for your app [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/same-instance-only.html#what-that-means-for-your-app)

- Your app must live on the same GitLab instance that hosts this project; if it does not, the components cannot run here.
- git.wayne.edu now has an instance runner, and the stack's CI runs on it. Every product in the stack still strongly recommends a git.wayne.edu instance runner, so that capacity stays there. See [Strongly recommended: a git.wayne.edu instance runner](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/instance-runner.html).
- A package that is also mirrored to `github.com/waynestate` cannot include the components there, because GitHub is not a GitLab instance at all. For those mirrors, Preflight ships a reusable GitHub Actions workflow that runs the same checks: the package's `composer ci` script on each supported PHP version, plus a Composer audit. See [GitHub mirrors](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/github-mirrors.html).

### Mirroring is the only exception [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/same-instance-only.html#mirroring-is-the-only-exception)

The one way to use the components on another GitLab instance is mirroring: mirror this project to that instance, so the components live there too. Everything else in this manual assumes the app and the components share an instance.

### Related [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/same-instance-only.html#related)

- [GitHub mirrors](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/github-mirrors.html): the reusable GitHub Actions workflow for packages mirrored to `github.com/waynestate`.
- [Strongly recommended: a git.wayne.edu instance runner](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/instance-runner.html): where the stack's CI runs, and why the recommendation stays.
- [When the components run](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/when-components-run.html): the `workflow:rules` block that belongs in the app's own file.

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/template-lint.html

## Template lint [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/template-lint.html#template-lint)

This page lists the unsafe CI patterns the template lint catches and how to allowlist a known warning. Run `composer ci` to see the lint, which runs before the fixture tests.

### What it runs [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/template-lint.html#what-it-runs)

`composer ci` runs `bin/lint-templates` before the fixture tests. The lint scans `templates/**/*.yml` and `.github/workflows/*.yml` for unsafe CI patterns.

### Rules [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/template-lint.html#rules)

| Rule | Catches |
| --- | --- |
| `privileged` | `privileged: true` |
| `dind-service` | Docker-in-Docker services |
| `docker-sock` | references to `docker.sock` |
| `kaniko-image` | Kaniko images |
| `unpinned-action` | GitHub `uses:` entries that are not pinned to a 40-character SHA |
| `image-no-tag` | image references with no tag |
| `image-latest` | image references with `latest` |
| `image-no-digest` | a warning for a tagged image that is not pinned by digest |

The container-build rules (`privileged`, `dind-service`, `docker-sock` and `kaniko-image`) are explained in BEST_PRACTICES.md 4.17.

### Allowlist a known warning [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/template-lint.html#allowlist-a-known-warning)

Known warnings can be allowlisted in `lint-allow.yml`. Each entry needs `file`, `rule` and `reason`; the reason is required so an allowlist entry is a reviewed decision, not a silence. The preflight checklist checks the checklist.

### Related [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/template-lint.html#related)

- [Updating image pins](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/image-pins.html): why component images are digest-pinned and how to change a pin.
- [Shared conventions](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/conventions.html): Composer vendor, license, PHP floor and JavaScript installs.

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-components-cannot-force.html

## What the components cannot force [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-components-cannot-force.html#what-the-components-cannot-force)

An included component is a set of ordinary jobs. The app's own `.gitlab-ci.yml` is merged over them, so an app can override a job's keys, skip it with `rules`, or delete the `include:` line. Preflight makes the safe pipeline the easy one; it does not lock it. Rollcall is where skipped or weakened gates will show up. A preflight checklist only works if the pilot reads it. This page lists which jobs may be allowed to fail and the five project settings that make the gates harder to skip.

### Which jobs may be allowed to fail [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-components-cannot-force.html#which-jobs-may-be-allowed-to-fail)

Four components take an `allow_failure` input, all defaulting to `false`: `proctor`, `secret-detection`, `a11y` and `squire-kit`. A policy finding is a warning while an app adopts PROCTOR's rules, a secret finding while a repo allowlists its first false positives, an accessibility finding while a site fixes what the gate found on its first run, and a kit finding while a repo puts its deploy kit back to Squire's files, so each job may fail without failing the pipeline during adoption; the first three still write their reports. `composer-audit` and `npm-audit` have no such input on purpose: a known advisory must fail the pipeline. The other jobs have no `allow_failure` input either.

No template adds a global key such as `default:`, `variables:`, `workflow:` or `stages:`. `tests/check-contract.sh` (and its `.ps1` twin) fails on any top-level key in a template that is not a job named in `contract/inputs.json`, so a global key fails `composer ci`.

### Protection checklist [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-components-cannot-force.html#protection-checklist)

A pilot signs each line of the checklist; the plane does not sign for you. Five project settings make the gates harder to skip, and every one of them works on GitLab Community Edition:

- [ ] **Protect the default branch** and require a merge request to change it. Every change to `.gitlab-ci.yml` then gets a reviewer. (Code owner approval needs Premium, so on Community Edition the reviewer is whoever merges.)
- [ ] **Protect the release tags.** Protect `*` or the release tag pattern so only maintainers can create or move a tag. A component ref is a tag, so whoever can move it controls every pipeline that pins it.
- [ ] **Set merge request approvals to at least one** for changes to the default branch. Approvals are available on every tier, but code owner rules within them need Premium, so on Community Edition the approval rests with whoever has merge rights: rely on the merger as the reviewer.
- [ ] **Set "Minimum role to use pipeline variables" to `no_one_allowed`** unless the project needs pipeline variables. The components take inputs, which are fixed and type checked for the whole run. Self-managed GitLab defaults this setting to `maintainer`.
- [ ] **Keep secrets away from fork merge requests.** A fork's merge request pipeline runs the fork's configuration. Review a fork's `.gitlab-ci.yml` before running its pipeline, and never give it protected variables.

Note

These are project settings Preflight cannot create or check, and a read-only token drift report was considered and left out on purpose: it would trade a token for a warning, and the checklist costs nothing to keep.

### Related [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-components-cannot-force.html#related)

- [When the components run](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/when-components-run.html)
- [The job token allowlist](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/job-token-allowlist.html)
- [GitHub mirrors](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/github-mirrors.html)

## When the components run [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/when-components-run.html#when-the-components-run)

The components are ordinary jobs, so they run whenever the app's pipeline runs. This page shows the `workflow:rules` block that runs them on every merge request and on pushes to the default branch, and why that block must live in the app's own file.

### The workflow:rules block [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/when-components-run.html#the-workflow-rules-block)

To run the components on every merge request and on pushes to the default branch, put a `workflow:rules` block in the app's own `.gitlab-ci.yml`:

```yaml
workflow:
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH

include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/proctor@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/composer-audit@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/sbom@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/pint@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/phpstan@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/eslint@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
```

Note

The `workflow:rules` block must live in the app's own file. A component cannot set the pipeline's `workflow:rules` for the project that includes it, so the `merge_request_event` rule goes in the app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`.

### Related [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/when-components-run.html#related)

- [Quick start](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html)

[![Preflight's front page: the headline Preflight, 'Every push is cleared for takeoff.', the include block for the php-test component, and the runway mark set in a heading-indicator instrument.](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/hero.jpg)](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/index.html)

## Preflight [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#preflight)

![php ^8.3](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/badges/php.svg) ![license MIT](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/badges/license.svg) ![gitlab ci components: 13](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/badges/components.svg)

**Every push is cleared for takeoff.**

Preflight is a set of GitLab CI/CD components that give every WSU app the same checks: PROCTOR, PHP tests on each supported version, Composer audit, an SBOM, Pint, PHPStan and ESLint. One include per component, pinned to a commit SHA, and the same checklist flies on every push.

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
    inputs:
      test_command: vendor/bin/phpunit
```

### Pick your path [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#pick-your-path)

- [Quick start](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html): wire one component into an app and watch the pipeline run it.
- [Install](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html): the requirements, the include snippet, and how to verify the pipeline picked the component up.
- [Reference](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html): every component, with its include example, inputs and defaults.

Preflight 0.5.0; GitLab components are GA on the Free tier since GitLab 17.0; MIT licensed.

Agents: fetch [https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt) for a machine-readable index of this manual.

---

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html

## Install [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#install)

Preflight installs as an `include:` in the app's own `.gitlab-ci.yml`, one line per component, pinned to a commit SHA with the tag in a trailing comment. A tag or branch can move; a SHA cannot.

### Requirements [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#requirements)

- GitLab 17.0 or newer. Components are GA on the Free tier since GitLab 17.0.
- Same instance only. Components work only within the same GitLab instance that hosts this project; they cannot be used across instances except by mirroring.

### Install [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#install-1)

Add the include to the app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`:

All seven components

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/proctor@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/composer-audit@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/sbom@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/pint@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/phpstan@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/eslint@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
```

One component

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
    inputs:
      test_command: vendor/bin/phpunit
```

### Verify [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#verify)

Push the change. The components are ordinary jobs, so they run whenever the app's pipeline runs, and each one lands in the `test` stage by default. Expected result: the pipeline shows the component's job, and for `php-test` that is one job per entry of `php_versions`, `8.3`, `8.4` and `8.5` by default. A green job means the check passed.

### Next steps [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#next-steps)

- [Quick start](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html): the same install as numbered steps with expected results.
- [When the components run](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/when-components-run.html): the `workflow:rules` block that belongs in the app's own file.
- [The php-test component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-php-test.html): inputs, caching, and trying the next PHP release.
