## Troubleshooting [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#troubleshooting)

What to do when a Preflight job fails or a gate behaves unexpectedly. Each entry names the cause, the fix, and how to check it. Most failures are a pin that moved or a setting that is missing. The checklist catches the rest.

Tip

Start with the job log. The message usually names the input that is wrong, and every input is listed on the [Components](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html) page.

### The pipeline [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-pipeline)

#### The include fails on another GitLab instance [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-include-fails-on-another-gitlab-instance)

Components work only inside the GitLab instance that hosts this project, and they cannot be used across instances except by mirroring.

- **Cause:** the app lives on a different instance than the one that hosts Preflight.
- **Fix:** host the app on the same instance. For a package that is also mirrored to GitHub, use the reusable workflow at `.github/workflows/php-package.yml` in this repo instead of the components.
- **Check:** the include path starts with `$CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/`, and the app's project is on that same instance.

#### The components do not run on merge requests [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-components-do-not-run-on-merge-requests)

The components are ordinary jobs, so they run whenever the app's pipeline runs. Whether the pipeline runs on a merge request is decided by a `workflow:rules` block, and a component cannot set it for the project that includes it.

- **Cause:** the app's own `.gitlab-ci.yml` has no `workflow:rules` block with a `merge_request_event` rule.
- **Fix:** add the block to the app's own file:

```yaml
workflow:
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH
```

- **Check:** a merge request pipeline runs, and so does a push to the default branch.

#### A gate was skipped or weakened [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#a-gate-was-skipped-or-weakened)

An included component is a set of ordinary jobs. The app's own `.gitlab-ci.yml` is merged over them, so an app can override a job's keys, skip it with `rules`, or delete the `include:` line. Preflight makes the safe pipeline the easy one. It does not lock it.

- **Cause:** a change in the app's own `.gitlab-ci.yml` overrides, skips or removes a component job.
- **Fix:** review the diff of the app's `.gitlab-ci.yml` against the last known-good pipeline, and restore the job or the `include:` line.
- **Check:** Rollcall is where skipped or weakened gates show up.

#### Two includes of the same component became one job [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#two-includes-of-the-same-component-became-one-job)

Every component takes a `job_name` input, whose default is the job's usual name. Without it, two includes of the same component share a job name and merge into one.

- **Cause:** one project includes the same component more than once (for example in a monorepo with two apps) without setting `job_name`.
- **Fix:** set `job_name` on each include, for example `pint-app` and `pint-admin`. `job_name` ships in 0.1.4, so pin 0.1.4 or a SHA at or after that release.
- **Check:** the pipeline lists one job per include, with the names you set.

#### Pipeline creation fails on the unknown `spec: component:` key [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#pipeline-creation-fails-on-the-unknown-spec-component-key)

Every Preflight component declares `spec: component:`, and GitLab only accepts that key from 18.7 on. On an older instance the pipeline never starts: creation fails with "header:spec config contains unknown keys".

- **Cause:** the GitLab instance is older than 18.7.
- **Fix:** upgrade GitLab to 18.7 or later, or pin an older Preflight tag that does not declare `spec: component:`.
- **Check:** the instance banner shows 18.7 or later, and the pipeline creates and runs the component jobs.

#### A fork merge request ran with protected variables [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#a-fork-merge-request-ran-with-protected-variables)

A fork's merge request pipeline runs the fork's configuration.

- **Cause:** the project lets fork pipelines see protected variables.
- **Fix:** review a fork's `.gitlab-ci.yml` before running its pipeline, and never give it protected variables.
- **Check:** the fork pipeline's variable list does not include any protected variable.

### Job failures [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#job-failures)

#### A job misbehaves: which Preflight release ran? [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#a-job-misbehaves-which-preflight-release-ran)

Every Preflight job prints a `Preflight component <name> <version> (ref <reference>, sha <sha>)` line before any other command. When a job fails or behaves unexpectedly, read that first line to see which Preflight release produced it: `<name>` is the component, `<version>` the pinned release tag, `<reference>` the ref the include points at, and `<sha>` the commit SHA of the template that ran. Compare it with the pin in the app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`; a mismatch means the include moved or the pipeline ran on an older pin.

- **Cause:** the job log does not say which Preflight release ran, so the failure cannot be tied to a pin.
- **Fix:** read the `Preflight component` line at the top of the job log. If the line is missing, the include is pinned to a Preflight release from before the line shipped; pin the current tag.
- **Check:** the first line of the job log names the component, its version, reference and SHA, and they match the pin in the app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`.

#### PROCTOR's preflight-pinned check warns [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#proctor-s-preflight-pinned-check-warns)

A tag or branch can move. A SHA cannot. PROCTOR's `preflight-pinned` check warns when an include is not pinned to a commit SHA.

- **Cause:** the include is pinned to a tag or a branch instead of a full commit SHA.
- **Fix:** pin the full commit SHA and keep the tag in a trailing comment, as in the examples on the [Components](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html) page.
- **Check:** PROCTOR's report no longer carries the `preflight-pinned` finding.

#### composer-audit is green, then an advisory lands [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#composer-audit-is-green-then-an-advisory-lands)

New advisories are published after code is merged, so a green pipeline today can be stale tomorrow.

- **Cause:** no pipeline has run since the advisory was published.
- **Fix:** create a weekly pipeline schedule on the default branch: project settings, Build, Pipeline schedules. The component needs nothing extra. It carries no `rules:` block, so it runs in scheduled pipelines like any other. Someone with Maintainer rights on the app creates the schedule.
- **Check:** the schedule appears under project settings, Build, Pipeline schedules, and its latest pipeline is green.

#### composer-audit fails on an abandoned package [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#composer-audit-fails-on-an-abandoned-package)

The job log names an abandoned package in the lock. An abandoned package is one its author no longer maintains, and `composer audit` fails the job on one by default.

- **Cause:** the lock holds a package marked abandoned, and the `abandoned` input is at its default, `fail`.
- **Fix:** upgrade the package or move to its successor where the log names one. While that is not possible, set the `abandoned` input on the include: `report` lists the abandoned packages without failing the job (right for an old app with abandoned transitive packages), `ignore` does not look at them at all. Advisories still fail the job in every mode.
- **Check:** with `report`, the job is green and its log lists the abandoned packages; with `fail`, the job fails until the lock no longer holds one.

#### npm-audit fails with "audit endpoint returned an error" [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#npm-audit-fails-with-audit-endpoint-returned-an-error)

The job log ends with `npm-audit: the registry's audit endpoint could not be reached or refused the request, so nothing was audited.`

- **Cause:** the runner cannot reach the npm registry over HTTPS, or the app's `.npmrc` names a registry that does not serve npm's audit endpoints (`/-/npm/v1/security/advisories/bulk`).
- **Fix:** let the runner reach the registry the log names, or point the audit at one that serves the endpoints. The job never passes without an answer.
- **Check:** the job log shows npm's report (`found 0 vulnerabilities` or a list) instead of the error.

#### npm-audit fails on a dev-only package [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#npm-audit-fails-on-a-dev-only-package)

- **Cause:** `omit_dev` is `false`, so the gate audits dev dependencies too.
- **Fix:** upgrade the package, or leave `omit_dev` at its default, `true`: the gate then reads runtime dependencies only, and the full report after it still lists the dev finding without failing.
- **Check:** the gate's lines say `failing on high or higher in runtime dependencies`.

#### composer install stops: the lock needs another PHP or an extension [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#composer-install-stops-the-lock-needs-another-php-or-an-extension)

The job log stops at `composer install` with `your php version (8.4.x) does not satisfy that requirement`, or with `requires ext-gd * -> it is missing from your system` (gd, oci8 and ldap are the usual ones). The `php-test`, `pint` and `phpstan` jobs install the app to run it, so they need what the app needs.

- **Cause:** the lock was built for an older PHP, or the app needs a PHP extension that the default image does not have. The default `php:*-cli` and `composer` images carry only the extensions PHP builds in.
- **Fix:** for an old PHP, upgrade the app: that red job is the finding, not a fault in Preflight. For an extension, set the job's `image` input to an image that has the same extensions as the app's Citadel image, for example one built `FROM php:8.4-cli-trixie` with `docker-php-ext-install gd`. The `proctor` and `sbom` jobs never run the app, so they install with `--ignore-platform-reqs` and need neither.
- **Check:** the `composer install` step of the job passes, and the job fails, if at all, on its own check.

#### composer install cannot clone a private package [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#composer-install-cannot-clone-a-private-package)

The job log shows `Failed to execute git clone --mirror` for a repository on the app's own GitLab instance, or `Could not connect to server`.

- **Cause:** the lock installs a package straight from a private Git repository, and the job has no credential for it. A local `auth.json` never reaches CI.
- **Fix:** give Composer a credential in the pipeline, for example a masked CI/CD variable `COMPOSER_AUTH` holding an `http-basic` entry for the instance with a deploy token that can read the package's project. Prefer publishing the package to the GitLab package registry and listing only that project in the job token allowlist; see [Keep the job token allowlist short](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/job-token-allowlist.html).
- **Check:** the `composer install` step passes in a pipeline on a branch.

#### eslint stops at npm ci [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#eslint-stops-at-npm-ci)

The `eslint` job stops at `npm ci` with the usage text, before ESLint runs.

- **Cause:** `npm ci` needs a `package-lock.json`, and the app keeps only a `yarn.lock` or a `pnpm-lock.yaml`.
- **Fix:** commit a `package-lock.json` (run `npm install` once), or leave the `eslint` component out until the app moves to npm.
- **Check:** `npm ci --ignore-scripts` passes locally from a clean checkout.

#### php-test-next is red [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#php-test-next-is-red)

A red `php-test-next` job is an early warning, not a stop. It is the second `php-test` include that tries the PHP release that is not supported yet, with `allow_failure: true` in the app's own file.

- **Cause:** the next PHP release still fails the app's tests, or only has release candidate images.
- **Fix:** leave `allow_failure: true` in place while the release is unsupported. Once the release is supported (the supported versions follow `policy.json`), drop the `allow_failure` and move the version into the main `php_versions` list.
- **Check:** the main `php-test` matrix is green. Only the named `php-test-next` job is red.

#### package-publish refuses the tag [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#package-publish-refuses-the-tag)

The job reads the registry before publishing. Republishing a version from the same commit is a no-op, and republishing it from a different commit fails instead of overwriting the version, because GitLab would otherwise overwrite it without a word.

- **Cause:** the tag's version already exists in the group's Composer registry, published from a different commit.
- **Fix:** publish a new version tag instead of moving the old one. Protect the release tags so only maintainers can create or move a tag.
- **Check:** the job log shows the version already on the manifest and the commit it was published from.

#### portability says an input is unknown [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#portability-says-an-input-is-unknown)

The one-job `portability` component has new inputs, and `buildah_image` is now `image` (the old app-image input is gone).

- **Cause:** the include is pinned to 0.1.4, which carries the two-job form (`portability-build`, `portability-run`, goss), or the include still sets `buildah_image`.
- **Fix:** pin a SHA at or after the one-job form and follow [Upgrading](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html): `buildah_image` becomes `image`, and the old app `image` input is gone because nothing is pushed.
- **Check:** the pipeline lists one job, `portability`.

#### portability fails before the build on the runner [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#portability-fails-before-the-build-on-the-runner)

Buildah's chroot isolation opens a user namespace.

- **Cause:** the runner (or Docker's seccomp profile on a laptop) refuses user namespaces; the log shows `unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER): Operation not permitted`.
- **Fix:** run the job on a runner that permits user namespaces, which ordinary unprivileged Docker-executor runners do. Do not make the runner privileged for it. Locally, add `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined` to `docker run`.
- **Check:** the log reaches `buildah bud` and prints the build steps.

#### portability: health: FAIL on a Laravel app [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#portability-health-fail-on-a-laravel-app)

The probe asks for the health path with a bare IP address in `Host` (`Host: <ip>:<port>`), the way a platform's probe does.

- **Cause:** the trusted-hosts middleware, an HTTPS redirect, a session or an auth check runs before the health route.
- **Fix:** answer the health route before those, for example Laravel's `health: '/up'` route in `bootstrap/app.php`, and exempt it from trusted hosts and HTTPS redirects.
- **Check:** `portability: health: pass`.

#### portability: sigterm: FAIL [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#portability-sigterm-fail)

The main process must handle SIGTERM and exit by itself within `stop_timeout`, because PID 1 ignores a signal it has no handler for.

- **Cause:** the image `exec`s a server that has no SIGTERM handler (for example `php -S`), or a shell script starts the server without passing the signal on.
- **Fix:** start the app under an init that forwards signals (`tini`, `dumb-init`) or a server that handles SIGTERM itself (php-fpm, FrankenPHP); in a shell entrypoint, trap TERM and stop the child.
- **Check:** `portability: sigterm: pass` with `handled SIGTERM and exited by itself`.

#### portability: an Apache image fails after the upgrade to 0.5.0 [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#portability-an-apache-image-fails-after-the-upgrade-to-0-5-0)

Since 0.5.0 the job gives each replica stdio its uid owns and a session of its own, so the `start_command` shim older releases needed is in the way.

- **Cause:** `start_command` still runs `setsid` (for example `exec setsid bash -c 'exec > >(exec cat) 2>&1; exec squire-entrypoint'`). Inside the job's launcher the shell already leads its own session, so `setsid` forks the app away from the replica's main process, and the replica never answers: `health` fails with `last answer: 000`.
- **Fix:** delete the `start_command` input, so the job runs the image's own `ENTRYPOINT` and `CMD`.
- **Check:** `portability: health: pass` and `portability: sigterm: pass`.

#### portability: session-hop: FAIL with "set session_login_path" [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#portability-session-hop-fail-with-set-session-login-path)

`session-hop` needs a route that signs in a test user and one that answers 200 only for a signed-in user.

- **Cause:** `session_login_path` and `session_check_path` are empty, but `session-hop` is in `checks`.
- **Fix:** add the two routes behind an environment variable only the job sets (see [The portability component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-portability.html#a-sign-in-route-for-session-hop)), or, for an app with no sign-in, leave `session-hop` out of `checks`.
- **Check:** `portability: session-hop: pass`, or `skipped` when left out on purpose.

#### a11y fails on a page that looked fine [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#a11y-fails-on-a-page-that-looked-fine)

The job checks each page in light and dark mode at 320 px and 1280 px, with reduced motion, so it sees layouts and palettes a quick look in one browser misses.

- **Cause:** a fault that shows in one mode only, and the failing test case names that mode, for example `docs/index.html dark 320px`: a dark palette with weak contrast, a label hidden at phone width, or a fixed-width element that makes the page scroll sideways at 320 px (`preflight-reflow`, which names the element where the overflow starts).
- **Fix:** open the page in that mode (dark color scheme, a 320 px window) and fix the element the report names; each axe-core rule links its help page. While a site works through its first findings, set `allow_failure: true` on the include and remove it once the job is green.
- **Check:** the job's last line reads `a11y: clean`, and the merge request's test summary shows every case passing.

#### a11y stops with a configuration error (exit 2) [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#a11y-stops-with-a-configuration-error-exit-2)

Exit 2 means the job never judged a page: an input or a tool is wrong.

- **Cause:** one of the messages below.
  - `no file under site matches the page pattern ...`: a glob in `pages` matched nothing, often because the docs folder moved. A literal page that is missing fails its check with HTTP 404 instead.
  - `site folder not found`: `site_dir` does not exist in the job, for example because the site is built in another job and not passed as an artifact.
  - `cannot read the Playwright version from the image tag`: `image` was overridden with an image whose tag does not carry `vX.Y.Z`.
  - `Chromium did not start`: the playwright npm version does not match the browsers in the image.
  - `axe-core X ran, but axe_core_version is Y`: `axe_playwright_version` names a bridge whose axe-core range does not include `axe_core_version`.
- **Fix:** correct the input the message names: fix the glob or `site_dir`, set `playwright_version` to the Playwright release in the image, or move `axe_core_version` and `axe_playwright_version` together (Renovate bumps them as one group).
- **Check:** the job log's second line names the site or URL and the Playwright version, and the summary line names the axe-core version that ran.

#### squire-kit fails: the kit drifted (exit 1) [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#squire-kit-fails-the-kit-drifted-exit-1)

The job installs the Squire release the kit records and runs `squire init --check`; the log lists every kit file with its state.

- **Cause:** one of the states below.
  - `modified`: someone, or a bot, edited a file Squire owns. Renovate's digest and tag bumps to `.squire/` files and `docker-compose.squire.yml` were the usual culprit before the preset turned them off.
  - `outdated`: the file is untouched but is not the template of the recorded release, usually because `.squire.json` was bumped without `squire update`.
  - `missing`: a kit file is gone, or the release added one that `squire update` does not write.
  - `untracked`: a file sits in one of the kit's groups but is not recorded in `.squire.json`.
- **Fix:** for `outdated` and `missing`, run `vendor/bin/squire update --path=deploy`, then `vendor/bin/squire init --path=deploy`, review the diff and commit it. For `modified`, put Squire's file back with `vendor/bin/squire init --force --path=deploy` and send the change to Squire instead, so every kit gets it. While a repository works through its first findings, set `allow_failure: true` on the include and remove it once the job is green.
- **Check:** `vendor/bin/squire init --check --path=deploy` prints `RESULT: pass`, and so does the job's last line.

#### squire-kit stops before checking (exit 2) [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#squire-kit-stops-before-checking-exit-2)

Exit 2 means the job never compared a file.

- **Cause:** one of the messages below.
  - `no .squire.json in ...`: `working_dir` is not the kit folder. The stack's repos keep the kit in `deploy`.
  - `.squire.json records no released Squire version`: the manifest is damaged or records a branch.
  - `could not install waynestate/squire X from Packagist`: no such release, or the job cannot reach Packagist.
- **Fix:** set `working_dir` to the folder holding `.squire.json`, set `squire_version` to the release the kit was written with, or let the job reach Packagist.
- **Check:** the job log prints `Checking the kit in ... against Squire X` before the file list.

### Renovate [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#renovate)

#### Renovate sees literal text instead of a token [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#renovate-sees-literal-text-instead-of-a-token)

On GitLab 19.5 a self-reference such as `RENOVATE_TOKEN: $RENOVATE_TOKEN` in the job `variables:` arrives as literal text and shadows the masked project CI/CD variables. The component does not map either token on purpose. The job reads both straight from the project.

- **Cause:** the runner project, or the app's file, adds `RENOVATE_TOKEN: $RENOVATE_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_COM_TOKEN: $GITHUB_COM_TOKEN` to `variables:`.
- **Fix:** delete the self-reference. Keep `RENOVATE_TOKEN` (and optionally `GITHUB_COM_TOKEN`) as masked CI variables in the private runner project.
- **Check:** the job log no longer shows the literal text `$RENOVATE_TOKEN`, and Renovate authenticates.

#### Renovate auto-merged a component pin bump [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#renovate-auto-merged-a-component-pin-bump)

In refs before 0.1.4 the component-rule manager name in `renovate/default.json` did not match repository deps, so a bump of a `component:` include version auto-merged instead of waiting for review.

- **Cause:** the shared preset comes from a ref before the 0.1.4 fix.
- **Fix:** point the repositories' `renovate.json` at the shared preset from 0.1.4 or later. Component version bumps now carry the `needs-review` label and never auto-merge.
- **Check:** the merge request carries the `needs-review` label.

#### A Squire kit merge request shows an artifact error [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#a-squire-kit-merge-request-shows-an-artifact-error)

The preset's Squire rule runs two commands after it bumps `.squire.json`: it installs the new Squire into `/tmp` and runs `squire update` on the kit folder. The merge request reports an artifact error when it could not.

- **Cause:** the runner does not allow the commands (the message says the command `has not been added to the allowed list in allowedCommands`; the renovate component's `squire_kit_tasks` input is off), or `squire update` refused a kit file someone edited (the message names the file), or the release needs PHP or a network the runner lacks.
- **Fix:** check out the branch, run `vendor/bin/squire update --path=deploy` (and `vendor/bin/squire init --path=deploy` for a release that adds a file), review the diff and commit it to the branch. For an edited file, restore it first with `vendor/bin/squire init --force --path=deploy`. To let the runner do this itself, set `squire_kit_tasks: true` on its renovate include.
- **Check:** the `squire-kit` job on the merge request is green.

### Local checks [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#local-checks)

#### The portability fixtures fail with "buildah is required" [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-portability-fixtures-fail-with-buildah-is-required)

`tests/check-portability.sh` runs inside the component's Buildah image, not on the host.

- **Cause:** the script was run with `sh` on the host.
- **Fix:** run it through `docker run` in the Buildah image as [Local checks](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/local-checks.html) shows, or run `pwsh -File tests/check-portability.ps1` on Windows.
- **Check:** one result line per case, and the script exits 0.

#### composer ci fails on a stale docs site [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#composer-ci-fails-on-a-stale-docs-site)

`composer ci` runs `docs:check`, which fails when the built docs site is stale or the generated command or environment reference has drifted from the CLI or source.

- **Cause:** a page under `docs/` (or a generated reference) changed without rebuilding `site/docs/`.
- **Fix:** run `composer docs` to rebuild `site/docs/` from `docs/`, and commit the rebuilt site with the page.
- **Check:** `composer docs:check` passes.

## Upgrading [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#upgrading)

This page is the checklist for moving an app from one Preflight pin to the next, one released version at a time, newest first; every section follows `CHANGELOG.md`. Read the section for the version you are moving to, apply its steps, and verify on the next pipeline. Like a real preflight, the walk takes a few minutes and earns its keep: move the pin only after you have read the version notes.

Every input and job name a component offers is recorded in `contract/inputs.json`, and Preflight's build fails when a template drifts from it, so the file is the exact list of what moved. Before you move a pin, diff it between your tag and the next one (for example `git diff 0.4.0 0.5.0 -- contract/inputs.json` in a clone of Preflight) and check each line against that version's Breaking and Steps below. [The inputs contract](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/inputs-contract.html) explains what each kind of change means for your include.

### 0.5.0 [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-5-0)

Released 2026-11-09. A new component, `npm-audit`, the front-end half of `composer-audit`; a portability probe that starts each replica the way a container runtime does, so an Apache image needs no `start_command` shim; a proctor job that keeps PROCTOR's JSON report as `proctor.json` for Rollcall; and Composer 2.11.1 in every default. No input or job was renamed or removed.

#### Breaking [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#breaking)

**The portability launcher.** The `portability` job now starts each replica through a launcher that gives it stdout and stderr its uid owns and a session of its own (`setsid`), as a container runtime does. An include that still carries a `start_command` shim calling `setsid` (WELD's was `exec setsid bash -c '...'`) breaks on 0.5.0: inside the launcher the shim forks the app away from the replica's main process, and `health` fails. Delete the shim in the same change as the bump. With an empty `start_command` the job runs the image's own `ENTRYPOINT` and `CMD`, which is what an Apache image (Squire's portable image, a Sourdough or WELD app) needs. A `start_command` that only starts the app, with no `setsid` and no stdio redirect, keeps working.

#### Deprecated [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#deprecated)

Nothing was deprecated in 0.5.0.

#### Changed [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#changed)

- **Composer 2.11.1.** Every Composer default moves from 2.10.3 to 2.11.1: the `composer-audit`, `sbom`, `pint`, `phpstan`, `package-publish` and `squire-kit` images are `composer:2.11.1@sha256:8de2184c...` (the multi-arch list digest), and php-test's and proctor's `composer_version` default is `2.11.1`. 2.11.0 fixed GHSA-c968-33g3-wh7p and GHSA-fm2w-xgf2-f9fh, and 2.10 is no longer maintained. 2.11 drops the `source-fallback` setting; no component sets it. An include that sets `image` or `composer_version` keeps its own pin.
- **proctor keeps `proctor.json`.** The proctor job's artifact now keeps PROCTOR's JSON report as `proctor.json` for 30 days, next to the Code Quality report, whether the job passed or failed. That is the file Rollcall reads with `ROLLCALL_PROCTOR_SOURCE=gitlab`. The job adds `--record "$CI_PROJECT_DIR/proctor.json"` itself, and only when `proctor_command` is a plain `proctor check` line and the app's PROCTOR is 0.11.0 or later. On PROCTOR 0.10.0 or older the job runs exactly as before and the runner warns that `proctor.json` matched no files. The proctor line's exit code still decides the job.
- **renovate's `dry_run` pattern is on record.** `contract/inputs.json` now lists the `^(null|lookup|full)$` pattern the renovate template already enforced in 0.4.0, so the contract diff shows that line changed. No value that passed on 0.4.0 stops passing.

#### New: npm-audit [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#new-npm-audit)

The `npm-audit` component runs `npm audit` on the app's `package-lock.json` in the `eslint` component's Node image and fails on an advisory at or above `audit_level` in a runtime dependency, then prints a full report that never fails. It is opt-in. Its inputs and defaults:

- `audit_level`: `high` by default; `low`, `moderate`, `high` or `critical`. CREED's and Composer's word `medium` is accepted too and maps to npm's `moderate`.
- `omit_dev`: `true` by default, so the failing audit leaves dev dependencies out; the full report still lists them.
- `working_dir`: `.` by default; the directory that holds `package-lock.json`, relative to the project root.
- `stage`, `job_name`, `image` and `image_prefix`, as on the other components.

An app with no lock file (no `package-lock.json` or `npm-shrinkwrap.json`) passes with a note, `npm-audit: no lock file ... nothing to audit.`, so a PHP-only app never goes red. An unreachable registry fails the job. See [The npm-audit component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-npm-audit.html).

#### Steps [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps)

1. If an include of `portability` sets a `start_command` shim that calls `setsid`, delete the shim (or the whole `start_command` line) in the same change as step 2.
2. Point each component include at the `0.5.0` tag, pinned to the tag's full commit SHA with the tag in a trailing comment:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
```

3. Optional: add `npm-audit` for an app with a front end:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/npm-audit@60314791565a264e97cb210813ef4f3e76512402 # 0.5.0
    inputs:
      audit_level: high
```

4. Optional: to feed Rollcall, move the app to PROCTOR 0.11.0 or later (`composer require --dev waynestate/proctor:^0.11`).

#### How to verify [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#how-to-verify)

The pipeline is green. The `portability` job passes all its checks with no shim, the composer-based jobs' `Pulling docker image` line names `composer:2.11.1`, and on PROCTOR 0.11.0 or later the proctor job's artifact holds `proctor.json`. With `npm-audit` included, its log ends with `npm audit`'s summary, or with the no-lock-file note. Checklist done, doors armed: cleared for takeoff.

### 0.4.0 [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-4-0)

Released 2026-11-08. Two new inputs and a Composer floor. The proctor component's `git_depth` (default `"0"`) clones the full history, so PROCTOR's override-approver check can read git blame on every override line instead of reporting could-not-run past GitLab's 20-commit default. php-test's `php_advisory_version` runs one more PHP version, such as a release candidate, in a separate job that may fail. php-test and proctor refuse a `composer_version` older than 2.9.6, the floor with the 2026 security fixes.

#### Breaking [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#breaking-1)

An include that sets `composer_version` on php-test or proctor to a version older than 2.9.6 no longer starts: GitLab rejects the input before the pipeline runs. The default (2.10.3) is unaffected, and no other input, default or job name changed.

#### Deprecated [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#deprecated-1)

Nothing was deprecated in 0.4.0.

#### Steps [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps-1)

1. If an include sets `composer_version` below 2.9.6, remove the input (the default is 2.10.3) or set 2.9.6 or later.
2. Point each component include at the `0.4.0` tag, pinned to the tag's full commit SHA with the tag in a trailing comment:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@87d9b6fc6b0ed302dd729986525282cd7b567ebd # 0.4.0
```

3. Optional: on a very large repository, set the proctor component's `git_depth` to a number such as `50`; override lines older than that then report could-not-run. To hear about the next PHP early, set php-test's `php_advisory_version`, for example `8.6.0RC2`.

#### How to verify [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#how-to-verify-1)

The pipeline is green, the proctor job log's fetch line no longer says `git depth set to 20` (unless you set `git_depth`), and with `php_advisory_version` set a `php-test-advisory` job runs and may fail without failing the pipeline.

### 0.3.1 [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-3-1)

Released 2026-11-08. Every component that installs packages caches under a fixed key per component (such as `preflight-pint`, or `preflight-php-8.4` for one PHP version of `php-test`) instead of a lock-file hash, and saves its cache even when the job fails. A lock change, or a retry after a dropped download, fetches only what is missing.

#### Breaking [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#breaking-2)

0.3.1 has no breaking changes: inputs, defaults and job names are the same as in 0.3.0.

#### Deprecated [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#deprecated-2)

Nothing was deprecated in 0.3.1.

#### Steps [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps-2)

Point each component include at the `0.3.1` tag, pinned to the tag's full commit SHA with the tag in a trailing comment:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@b90323b5823287a7840095d0d5f0682aaeedf327 # 0.3.1
```

The first pipeline on the new pin fills the new cache keys, so expect it to download everything once.

#### How to verify [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#how-to-verify-2)

The pipeline is green, and a component's job log shows `Creating cache preflight-` followed by the component's key, and, after a failed job, `Saving cache for failed job`.

### 0.3.0 [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-3-0)

Released 2026-11-08. Docker Hub images now come through the group's Dependency Proxy by default (a new `image_prefix` input), and more components cache their Composer and npm downloads.

#### Breaking [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#breaking-3)

Every component whose image comes from Docker Hub (`proctor`, `php-test`, `composer-audit`, `sbom`, `pint`, `phpstan`, `eslint`, `secret-detection`, `package-publish`, `renovate`, `squire-kit`) now pulls `image_prefix/image`, and `image_prefix` defaults to your group's Dependency Proxy (`${CI_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GROUP_IMAGE_PREFIX}`). `image` keeps its default and is the path after the prefix. Only an app that overrides `image`, or runs where the proxy is off, needs to act:

1. If the override was `${CI_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GROUP_IMAGE_PREFIX}/<image>` only to reach the proxy, delete the `image:` input; the default does the same. Keeping it puts the prefix in twice, and the pull fails.
2. If it names a different Docker Hub image, drop the `${CI_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GROUP_IMAGE_PREFIX}/` part and keep the rest.
3. If it names another registry, move the host and path into `image_prefix` and keep the rest in `image`.
4. On a GitLab or group without the proxy, set `image_prefix: docker.io`.

`a11y` (mcr.microsoft.com) and `portability` (quay.io) have no `image_prefix` and are unchanged: the proxy serves Docker Hub only.

#### Deprecated [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#deprecated-3)

Nothing was deprecated in 0.3.0.

#### Steps [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps-3)

1. Move every Preflight include to the `0.3.0` tag in one change, pinned to the tag's full commit SHA with the tag in a trailing comment, and remove any proxied `image:` input in the same change (step 1 above):
   ```yaml
   include:
     - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@23038dfe767f6ef60e3b2efca1128f53d9acdff7 # 0.3.0
   ```
   Before:
   ```yaml
     - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@<old SHA> # 0.2.0
       inputs:
         image: ${CI_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GROUP_IMAGE_PREFIX}/php:8.4-cli-trixie@sha256:<digest>
   ```
   After:
   ```yaml
     - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@23038dfe767f6ef60e3b2efca1128f53d9acdff7 # 0.3.0
       inputs:
         image: php:8.4-cli-trixie@sha256:<digest>
   ```
2. On a GitLab or group without the Dependency Proxy, add `image_prefix: docker.io` to each Docker Hub include's `inputs`.
3. A mirrored package moves the SHA in its GitHub workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) to the same commit.

Verify: the job log's `Pulling docker image` line shows the prefix once, and each job's first line (`Preflight component <name> ...`) shows the new ref and sha. See [Dependency caching](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/dependency-caching.html).

### 0.2.0 [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-2-0)

#### Breaking [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#breaking-4)

The `portability` component is now one job, `portability` (named by a new `job_name` input), instead of `portability-build` and `portability-run`, and it checks what ADR-0010 asks for instead of the goss list. It builds the image with Buildah and runs it in the same job, so nothing is pushed to the container registry and no app image is pulled. Only an app that already includes `portability` from 0.1.4 needs to act:

- `buildah_image` is renamed `image` (same default, the Buildah image pinned by digest); the old `image` input (the app image) is gone.
- `start_command` is optional: empty runs the image's own `ENTRYPOINT` and `CMD`, the way the platforms do. Keep it only if your image needs a different start.
- New inputs with defaults: `job_name`, `build_args`, `runtime_paths`, `port_env`, `env`, `stop_timeout`, `probe_path`, `identity_header`, `session_login_path`, `session_check_path`, `logs_path` and `checks`. Set `env` to what the app needs to boot (secrets from CI/CD variables), and either add a test sign-in route for `session-hop` or leave it out of `checks`.
- Anything that waited on `portability-run` with `needs:` now names `portability`.
- The app image needs no curl, sha256sum or tar any more; the probe runs outside it.

See [The portability component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-portability.html) for the six checks and how to fix each failure.

#### Changed [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#changed-1)

The Buildah image default (now the `portability` component's `image` input) moved from the plain version tag to the immutable tag `quay.io/buildah/stable:v1.43.5-immutable@sha256:7c2b605262748ace2c5c57c5550942d0adad57aec82ede3070927722306c0ffb`: Red Hat re-pushed the plain version tag and garbage-collected the old digest, so a pipeline pinned to it broke. If your app overrides it, point it at an `-immutable` tag pinned by digest too. The `composer-audit` component gains an `abandoned` input (`fail`, `report` or `ignore`) for how `composer audit` treats abandoned packages. No action needed: the default is `fail`, which is what the component already did, so existing pipelines behave exactly as before. A new `a11y` component checks a site's pages with axe-core in Playwright (WCAG 2.1 AA by default; add `wcag22aa` for 2.2 AA). It is opt-in: add its include to start the gate, with `allow_failure: true` while the site fixes its first findings. See [The a11y component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-a11y.html). Preflight's own local gate (`scripts/a11y.sh`, `scripts/a11y.ps1`) now runs the component's checker, at 320 px instead of 360 px, with the reflow check; `tools/a11y/` is gone. A new `squire-kit` component fails the pipeline when a Squire deploy kit drifts from the Squire release its `.squire.json` records (`squire init --check`). It is opt-in: run `vendor/bin/squire init --check --path=deploy` first, clean up what it reports, then add the include with `working_dir: deploy`. See [The squire-kit component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-squire-kit.html). The Renovate preset no longer updates files inside a Squire kit (`docker-compose.squire.yml` and `.squire/**`, outside Squire's own `templates/`): those bumps made every kit drift. Its Squire rule now runs `squire update` on the kit in the merge request it opens for a new Squire. The runner must allow those commands: set `squire_kit_tasks: true` on the runner project's `renovate` include. Until it does, each Squire merge request shows an artifact error and needs `vendor/bin/squire update --path=deploy` run by hand, as before. See [Squire kits](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html#squire-kits). This release needs GitLab 18.7 or later: every component now declares `spec: component:` and prints a `Preflight component` line as its first command, and GitLab accepts that spec key only from 18.7 on. On an older instance, pipeline creation fails on the unknown key, so upgrade GitLab or pin an older Preflight tag.

### 0.1.4 [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-4)

Released 2026-11-03. The new pieces are opt-in: the `portability` component, a `job_name` input on every component except `portability`, and a stricter Renovate preset.

#### Breaking [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#breaking-5)

0.1.4 has no breaking changes: the version adds a component, an input and preset rules, and removes nothing.

#### Deprecated [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#deprecated-4)

Nothing was deprecated in 0.1.4.

#### Steps [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps-4)

Point each component include at the `0.1.4` tag, pinned to the tag's full commit SHA with the tag in a trailing comment:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/proctor@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
```

A mirrored package pins the same SHA in its GitHub workflow:

```yaml
jobs:
  ci:
    uses: waynestate/preflight/.github/workflows/php-package.yml@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
```

Adopt the new pieces when you want them:

- **`portability`**: it ships in 0.1.4 and later (0.1.3 does not include it), so pin the `0.1.4` tag, or the full commit SHA of a commit at or after it. The build job needs a runner that permits user namespaces (Buildah uses unshare for its storage); the run job needs only the project's container registry and an app image that carries curl, sha256sum and tar.
- **`job_name`**: it ships in 0.1.4, so pin 0.1.4 or a SHA at or after that release. Set it when one project includes the same component more than once, for example in a monorepo with two apps; without it the two jobs would share a name and merge into one.
- **Renovate preset**: component version bumps now really wait for review instead of auto-merging (the component-rule manager name is `gitlabci`, matching repository deps), and a bump of the recorded Squire kit version carries the `squire-kit` label and never auto-merges; a person runs `squire update` to refresh the kit files.

Note

Pins change only through a reviewed merge request. A tag or branch can move; a SHA cannot.

#### How to verify [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#how-to-verify-3)

Push the change and run the app's pipeline. The components are ordinary jobs, so they run whenever the app's pipeline runs; expect the same jobs as before, green. PROCTOR's `preflight-pinned` check warns when an include is not pinned to a commit SHA. If you added `portability`, the `portability-run` job passes only when the image boots the strict way and the goss checks hold.

### 0.1.3 [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-3)

Released 2026-11-03. Two consumer-facing changes: the `proctor` component installs the app with `--no-plugins --no-scripts`, and the shared Renovate preset stopped auto-merging the pins that every pipeline runs.

#### Breaking [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#breaking-6)

0.1.3 has no breaking changes, but the `proctor` job now installs the app's dependencies with `composer install --no-plugins --no-scripts`, so the app's plugins and scripts never run inside the job.

#### Deprecated [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#deprecated-5)

Nothing was deprecated in 0.1.3.

#### Steps [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps-5)

Bump each component include to the `0.1.3` tag's full commit SHA, with the tag in a trailing comment:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/proctor@<full commit SHA> # 0.1.3
```

If your group runs the shared Renovate preset, read the two behavior changes before you merge the bump:

- Updates inside `templates/**`, `contract/**` and `.gitlab-ci.yml`, and bumps of a Preflight component version in an app's `component:` include, no longer auto-merge: they carry the `needs-review` label and wait for a person.
- The `renovate` component no longer sets `RENOVATE_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_COM_TOKEN` from themselves in the job `variables:`; on GitLab 19.5 that self-reference arrived as literal text and shadowed the masked project CI/CD variables, so the job now reads both tokens straight from the project.

Warning

Do not add `RENOVATE_TOKEN: $RENOVATE_TOKEN` to your own `variables:`; that self-reference arrives as literal text.

#### How to verify [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#how-to-verify-4)

Run the pipeline and confirm the jobs run on the new pin. In the runner project, confirm the job reads `RENOVATE_TOKEN` straight from the project as a masked CI variable, and that a bump touching the templates, the contract or a component include pin opens a merge request labeled `needs-review` instead of auto-merging.

#### Breaking [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#breaking-7)

0.1.2 has no breaking changes: the version touches the site, the README and the proof page, not the components.

#### Deprecated [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#deprecated-6)

Nothing was deprecated in 0.1.2.

#### Steps [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps-6)

Bump each component include to the `0.1.2` tag's full commit SHA, with the tag in a trailing comment:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/proctor@<full commit SHA> # 0.1.2
```

#### How to verify [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#how-to-verify-5)

Run the pipeline and confirm the component jobs run on the new pin. PROCTOR's `preflight-pinned` check warns when an include is not pinned to a commit SHA.

### 0.1.1 [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-1)

Released 2026-10-29. Two new components: `package-publish`, which publishes a semantic version tag to the GitLab group's built-in Composer registry, and `renovate`, with the shared preset `renovate/default.json`. The reusable GitHub Actions workflow for mirrors ships in this tag too.

#### Breaking [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#breaking-8)

0.1.1 has no breaking changes: the version adds components and changes only the repository's own PHPStan config.

#### Deprecated [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#deprecated-7)

Nothing was deprecated in 0.1.1.

#### Steps [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps-7)

Bump the existing includes to the `0.1.1` tag's full commit SHA, and add the new components where you want them:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/package-publish@<full commit SHA> # 0.1.1
    inputs:
      group_id: "<your group id>"
```

`group_id` is required: the numeric id of the GitLab group whose built-in Composer registry hosts the package.

Warning

Protect your release tags. A component ref is a tag, so whoever can move it controls every pipeline that pins it.

A package mirrored to GitHub calls the reusable workflow from its own `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; the workflow ships in the `0.1.1` tag, so pin the full commit SHA of the release tag and keep the tag in a trailing comment:

```yaml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: ['**']
    tags: ['v*', '*.*.*']

jobs:
  ci:
    uses: waynestate/preflight/.github/workflows/php-package.yml@<full commit SHA> # 0.1.1
```

#### How to verify [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#how-to-verify-6)

Run the pipeline. For `package-publish`, the job runs only on tags and reads the registry first: a version already published from this commit passes quietly, and a version published from a different commit fails the pipeline. For a mirrored package, a release tag is not done until it is green on both sides.

### 0.1.0 [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-0)

Released 2026-10-27. First tagged release.

#### Breaking [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#breaking-9)

0.1.0 is the first tagged release, so there is nothing to break: it is the baseline every later pin moves from.

#### Deprecated [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#deprecated-8)

Nothing was deprecated in 0.1.0.

#### Steps [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps-8)

Include the components pinned to the `0.1.0` tag's full commit SHA:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/proctor@<full commit SHA> # 0.1.0
```

#### How to verify [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#how-to-verify-7)

Run the pipeline and confirm the component jobs run on the pin.
